items.title: [Bug]: tools.include/tools.exclude MCP filtering not enforced — blocked tools still callable via tool_describe and tool_call

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Bug Description

`mcp_servers.<name>.tools.include` / `tools.exclude` filtering is only applied at tool **registration** time (`_register_server_tools` in `tools/mcp_tool.py:5491`) but the **deferred tool catalog** used by `tool_describe` and the `tool_call` dispatch bridge is built from raw MCP discovery output — it never consults the per-server include/exclude filter.

**Result:** Blocked tools are invisible to the model in the system prompt (filtering works there) but remain fully discoverable via `tool_describe` and **callable via `tool_call`**. This means the filtering provides no security boundary — it is a model-awareness hint, not an access control.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a whitelist on any MCP server:
```yaml
mcp_servers:
  github:
    command: "npx"
    args: ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"]
    tools:
      include: [list_issues, create_issue, search_code]
      # merge_pull_request, delete_file, fork_repository are NOT in the list
```

2. `/reload-mcp` or restart Hermes.

3. Ask the model what GitHub tools it has → correctly reports only whitelisted tools.

4. Manually call a blocked tool via `tool_describe` or `tool_call`:
```python
tool_describe(name='mcp__github__merge_pull_request')
# → returns full schema (should error: "not available")

tool_call(name='mcp__github__merge_pull_request', arguments={...})
# → routes to GitHub API and executes (should be blocked)
```

5. Or use `tool_search` with `query='mcp__github__'` → blocked tools appear in results alongside whitelisted ones.

## Expected Behavior

`tools.include` should prevent blocked tools from being registered, discovered, or invoked through **any** path — `tool_describe`, `tool_search`, and `tool_call` included. The docs state: *"If `include` is set, only those server-native MCP tools are registered."*

## Actual Behavior

Blocked tools are reachable through the deferred tool bridge (`tool_describe` / `tool_call`) and the BM25 search catalog (`tool_search`). Only the system prompt (model's visible tool list) respects the filter.

## Root Cause Analysis

The filtering is applied in `_register_server_tools()` (`tools/mcp_tool.py:5515-5529`) which correctly skips blocked tools when calling `registry.register()`. But the deferred tool catalog is built from `current_tool_defs` — the raw MCP discovery output — in two places that never apply the filter:

1. **`tool_search.py:879-880`** — `build_catalog(deferrable)` where `deferrable` comes from `classify_tools(current_tool_defs)` — all discovered MCP tools, unfiltered.

2. **`tool_search.py:889-906`** — `dispatch_tool_describe()` iterates `classify_tools(current_tool_defs)` directly — again unfiltered.

The `_should_register()` logic (include/exclude with glob support and precedence rules) lives only in `mcp_tool.py` and is never consulted when building the deferred catalog or dispatching deferred tool calls.

## Impact

- **Security:** Tools excluded for safety reasons (`merge_pull_request`, `delete_file`, `archive_card`, `execute_workflow`, `publish_workflow`, etc.) remain callable through the bridge.
- **User trust:** Users who configure whitelists believing they have restricted tool access are unprotected.
- **Documentation gap:** The docs correctly describe intended behavior; the implementation doesn't match.

## Environment

- **Hermes version:** v0.19.0 (2026.7.20)
- **Config syntax:** Verified correct — YAML parse clean, gateway restarted
- Also confirmed non-functional on Hermes v0.17.0

## Proposed Fix Direction

The `current_tool_defs` list passed to the deferred tool catalog builder and `dispatch_tool_describe` needs to be filtered per-server using the same `_should_register()` logic from `mcp_tool.py`. This could be done by:

- Extracting the include/exclude filter into a shared utility
- Applying it when building `deferrable` in `classify_tools`
- Or filtering `current_tool_defs` before it reaches `build_catalog` and `dispatch_tool_describe`

## Related

- Docs reference: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/reference/mcp-config-reference#filtering-semantics
- Related security concern: #16462 (MCP tools bypass first-invoke approval)

items.title: Desktop pane freeze: Capabilities/Messaging/Artifacts only open once per session
items.body:
a/Desktop/hermes-bug-report.md → b/Desktop/hermes-bug-report.md
@@ -0,0 +1,23 @@
+### Describe the bug
+Capabilities, Messaging, and Artifacts panes only open once per desktop app session. After viewing one of these panes and then navigating away (e.g., back to Sessions), clicking them again does nothing — the pane won't re-render or show content. The only fix is to quit the app (Cmd+Q) and reopen it. After restart, the pane opens once, then the cycle repeats.
+
+The Sessions pane works fine — it opens/closes reliably across multiple navigations.
+
+### To Reproduce
+1. Open Hermes desktop app
+2. Click "Capabilities" (or "Messaging" or "Artifacts") — renders fine the first time
+3. Click "Sessions" to go back
+4. Click "Capabilities" again — nothing happens, pane stays on Sessions
+5. Quit and reopen — Capabilities works again (once)
+
+### Expected behavior
+Panes should re-render reliably every time they're clicked, not just once per session.
+
+### Environment
+- Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20)
+- macOS 26.5.2 (Apple Silicon M4)
+- Desktop app (Electron)
+- 103 skills, 5 MCP servers
+
+### Additional context
+This makes the app feel broken — users have to restart just to check their skills or messaging config. The issue is in the pane/view state management, not related to skill count or MCP count.

items.title: [Bug]: provider failover keeps the old provider's prompt-cache decoration (0 breakpoints after cache-off to cache-on failover)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P0
labels.description: Critical — data loss, security, crash loop

labels.name: sweeper:risk-caching
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break/degrade prompt caching or cache-key stability (invariant)

items.body:
### What happens

`try_activate_fallback` re-evaluates the prompt-cache policy for the new provider, but the request that goes out after the failover still carries the decoration built for the old one.

Decoration runs once per call block, before the retry loop, and the comment says as much ("Runs LAST, after every message mutation above"):

- `agent/conversation_loop.py:1566`: `api_messages = apply_anthropic_cache_control(...)`, guarded by `agent._use_prompt_caching`
- `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py:1838`: fallback activation refreshes `_use_prompt_caching` / `_use_native_cache_layout` for the new provider
- `agent/conversation_loop.py:4079`: the retry loop then `continue`s with the same `api_messages`. `_sync_failover_system_message` rewrites the system text but not the markers.

`apply_anthropic_cache_control` is never called again after a failover (zero call sites in chat_completion_helpers.py).

### What that costs, per policy transition

- cache-off primary to cache-capable fallback: the messages were never decorated, so the fallback runs with zero breakpoints. Full input-token price on every request for the rest of the conversation.
- cache-capable primary to cache-off fallback: stale `cache_control` fields are sent to a provider whose policy said no.
- native to envelope (or back): marker carrier eligibility differs (empty assistant/tool messages, `agent/prompt_caching.py:54`), so some of the four breakpoints sit where the new provider ignores them.
- One member that is easy to miss: a session restored under a cache-off primary never rebuilds `_cached_system_prompt_static` (`agent/conversation_loop.py:455`). If it later fails over to a cache-on provider, redecoration would get `static_system_prefix=None` and silently use the legacy system-plus-3 layout, even after a fix here.

### Why a one-line fix won't hold

There are nine same-list fallback continuation sites in conversation_loop.py that all reuse the current `api_messages`: 1870, 2269, 2342, 2506, 4079, 4112, 4643, 4866, 6252. Redecorating only the classified-error branch (4079) leaves the other eight paths sending the old layout.

Two more constraints for whoever picks this up:

- The decorated list is also mutated by the retry recoveries (surrogate/ASCII cleanup, image shrinking, reasoning_details removal: 3178, 3216, 3395, 3505, 3533, 3710, plus the 413 recovery at 4286). Rebuilding from a pristine pre-decoration snapshot would resurrect the un-shrunk images and get them rejected again. The redecoration source has to be the mutated, undecorated shape.
- MoA prepared requests ride the same list (`api_messages = _moa_prepared_request["messages"]`, `agent/conversation_loop.py:1600`) and their reference guidance is attached under a cache-stability contract (`agent/moa_loop.py:1318`). A naive strip-and-redecorate puts the last marker on the guidance block. That path needs `rebase_prepared_request` after decorating.

### Test gap

`tests/agent/test_failover_identity.py::TestSyncFailoverPreservesCacheDecoration` pins `native_anthropic=True` on both sides of the failover, so the policy-change class has no coverage today.

I'm filing the analysis instead of a PR: the correct fix looks like a single re-render chokepoint used by all nine sites, and that's not a small diff. Didn't want the findings to sit unreported in the meantime.

items.title: Desktop app shows "developer error" popup: gateway/WebSocket fails to connect (Windows, v0.19.0)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
On Windows, the **Hermes desktop client (Electron GUI)** repeatedly throws a startup/connection error dialog ("Something went wrong… developer error"). The underlying agent/gateway actually works fine — the failure is between the **Electron renderer** and the **local Python gateway backend**. Two deterministic bugs drive it:

1. **`event loop stalled` (GIL pressure) + WebSocket `ready frame send failed`** — the GUI↔backend keepalive dies under normal heavy load, and the GUI reports the backend as unreachable.
2. **`signal only works in main thread of the main interpreter`** — `tui_gateway` MCP discovery **crashes on every startup** (deterministic, not load-dependent).
3. **Bootstrap repair loop** — the desktop boot logic toggles `repair requested` ⇄ `reset requested` ⇄ `forcing reinstall` repeatedly and never stabilizes, and a **stale `gateway_state.json` (`running`) persists after the real PID is dead**, so the GUI won't restart the backend.

This is a **software bug, not a user/environment problem**: feishu connects (`✓ feishu connected`), config/.env are valid, and the agent itself responds normally.

## Environment

- OS: Windows 10 (host `20967`)
- Hermes desktop: bundled runtime `hermes-web-ui/desktop-runtime/hermes/0.19.0/win-x64`
- Two Python runtimes are being used to run the gateway:
  - `C:\Users\20967\.hermes-web-ui\desktop-runtime\hermes\0.19.0\win-x64\python\...` → **3.12.13** (desktop-launched gateway)
  - `C:\Users\20967\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\venv\Scripts\python.exe` → **3.11.15** (also launched gateway + `tui_gateway`)
- `config.yaml`: `model.default: tencent/hy3:free`, `model.provider: nous`
- Platforms: feishu connected (websocket mode)
- `_config_version: 33`

## Reproduction

1. Open the Hermes desktop app (or it auto-launches on boot).
2. Under normal usage — a long system prompt + ongoing tool calls (`execute_code`, sandbox, skill patches; model input ~87k tokens, output several thousand) — the error dialog appears.
3. The dialog is non-fatal: chat still works through the same backend, but the GUI keeps showing the error and the "repair" cycle loops.

Repro is intermittent on timing but the two code paths below fail **deterministically** on every launch.

## Evidence (from local logs)

### 1. WebSocket keepalive dies under GIL pressure (the visible "developer error")

`%LOCALAPPDATA%/hermes/logs/gui.log` (timestamps 2026-07-27, still reproducing today):

```
2026-07-27 19:34:11,657 WARNING hermes_cli.web_server: event loop stalled 54.0s (GIL pressure suspected)
2026-07-27 19:34:11,768 INFO tui_gateway.ws: ws accepted peer=127.0.0.1:2683
2026-07-27 19:34:11,786 WARNING tui_gateway.ws: ws send failed peer=127.0.0.1:2683 error_type=WebSocketDisconnect error=
2026-07-27 19:34:11,786 ERROR tui_gateway.ws: ws ready frame send failed peer=127.0.0.1:2683
2026-07-27 19:34:11,823 INFO tui_gateway.ws: ws closed peer=127.0.0.1:2683 reason=ready_send_failed messages=0 ... send_failures=1 ...

2026-07-27 19:37:27,170 WARNING hermes_cli.web_server: event loop stalled 61.8s (GIL pressure suspected)
2026-07-27 19:37:27,334 ERROR tui_gateway.ws: ws ready frame send failed peer=127.0.0.1:5902

2026-07-27 19:40:56,539 WARNING hermes_cli.web_server: event loop stalled 20.2s (GIL pressure suspected)
```

(The `event loop stalled … GIL pressure` warning also appears in `errors.log` at 12:02:36 / 12:12:45 with `ws ready frame send failed`.)

### 2. Deterministic gateway crash: `signal.signal` in non-main thread

`%LOCALAPPDATA%/hermes/logs/gui.log`:

```
2026-07-27 19:25:11,691 WARNING tui_gateway.server: MCP discovery startup failed
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "C:\Users\20967\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\tui_gateway\server.py", line 1866, in _build
    from tui_gateway.entry import ensure_mcp_discovery_started
  File "C:\Users\20967\AppData\Local\hermes\hermes-agent\tui_gateway\entry.py", line 190, in <module>
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, _log_signal)
  File "C:\Users\20967\AppData\Roaming\uv\python\cpython-3.11-windows-x86_64-none\Lib\signal.py", line 58, in signal
    handler = _signal.signal(_enum_to_int(signalnum), _enum_to_int(handler))
              ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
ValueError: signal only works in main thread of the main interpreter
```

This fires on **every** MCP discovery startup (also at 19:40:57). `signal.signal` is only valid in the main thread — it must not be called from a worker/async thread during `_build`.

### 3. Bootstrap repair loop + stale gateway state

`%LOCALAPPDATA%/hermes/logs/desktop.log` (repeats dozens of times):

```
[bootstrap] repair requested by renderer; clearing marker + latched failure
[boot] Restarting desktop connection
[bootstrap] repair requested; bypassing the usable active runtime to re-run the installer
[bootstrap] reset requested by renderer; clearing latched failure
[bootstrap] repair requested; forcing reinstall + clearing latched failure
...
[bootstrap] Active Hermes runtime at ...\hermes-agent is usable but the bootstrap marker is missing or stale; skipping first-run bootstrap.
```

`%LOCALAPPDATA%/hermes/gateway_state.json` shows `"gateway_state":"running"` with `pid:70244`, while that PID is **dead** (started 2026-07-26T10:28, a day before the still-failing session). The stale `running` marker prevents the GUI from relaunching the backend.

### 4. Other related defects observed in the same window

- `%LOCALAPPDATA%/hermes/logs/errors.log`:
  `Another gateway instance (PID 48344) started during our startup. Exiting to avoid double-running.` — startup race between two gateway launches.
- `%LOCALAPPDATA%/hermes/logs/errors.log`:
  `Could not restore async delegation completions: duplicate column name: origin_session_id` — internal state DB schema migration failure.
- Two different Python versions (3.11.15 vs 3.12.13) are both used to launch the gateway (see `gateway-exit-diag.log`), which can produce dependency mismatches (e.g. `lark_oapi` import failures).

## Root cause (hypothesis)

- The GUI's health check depends on a WebSocket `ready` frame over the **same asyncio event loop** that runs agent/model calls. Heavy synchronous/GIL-bound work (long prompts, `execute_code`) starves the loop, the `ready` frame can't be sent, and the GUI concludes the backend is down → "developer error" dialog.
- `tui_gateway/entry.py` installs a `SIGTERM` handler at import time (`signal.signal`) from a non-main thread during MCP discovery `_build`, which raises `ValueError` and aborts gateway bring-up.
- Bootstrap/repair state machine is fragile: a usable runtime is repeatedly treated as needing reinstall; `gateway_state.json` is not invalidated when the PID dies, so the "already running" guard blocks recovery.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Decouple the GUI keepalive from the agent event loop.** Run the desktop/WebSocket health server on its own loop/thread (or use a separate process), so model/GIL work can't stall the `ready` frame. Add a tolerant reconnect/backoff instead of an immediate error dialog.
2. **Fix the `signal.signal` call** in `tui_gateway/entry.py` — install `SIGTERM` only in the main thread (guard with `threading.current_thread() is threading.main_thread()` / `if sys.platform == "win32":` considerations), or move it to the entrypoint before spawning threads.
3. **Invalidate `gateway_state.json` on process exit / PID-not-alive check** so a dead PID doesn't block relaunch.
4. **Stop the bootstrap repair loop** — don't re-run the installer when an active, usable runtime already exists; clear the stale bootstrap marker deterministically.
5. **Serialize gateway startup** to remove the "Another gateway instance" double-launch race.
6. **Migrate/repair the internal state DB** so schema changes (e.g. `origin_session_id`) don't throw on restore.
7. **Pick one Python runtime** for the gateway (the 3.11.15 venv) and stop mixing it with the 3.12.13 desktop-runtime interpreter.

## Impact

- User-facing: recurring "developer error" popup; need to retry/repair; erodes trust.
- Functional: chat still works via the same backend, but MCP tool discovery crashes on every start, so MCP servers may not be available.

## Notes

- No user data loss: the error dialog itself states chats/settings are not deleted.
- Feishu connection is healthy (`✓ feishu connected`), confirming network/config are fine.
- Logs referenced (all under `%LOCALAPPDATA%/hermes/`): `logs/gui.log`, `logs/desktop.log`, `logs/errors.log`, `logs/gateway.log`, `gateway-exit-diag.log`, `gateway_state.json`.

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop slash/skill completion drawer doesn't scroll during keyboard navigation — highlight walks off-screen
items.body:
### Bug Description

In Hermes Desktop, the composer's completion drawer (the popup that recommends skills/slash commands when you type `/` — e.g. typing `./` in a message and continuing with a slash trigger) does not scroll along with keyboard navigation. Holding the **ArrowDown** key moves the highlighted row past the drawer's visible area: the drawer's scroll position stays frozen at the initial position, so the highlight walks off-screen and the currently selected item becomes impossible to observe. You can keep pressing ArrowDown and have no idea what you're about to accept with Enter/Tab.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Hermes Desktop and focus the chat composer.
2. Type `/` so the skill/command completion drawer opens with more items than fit in the drawer's max height (`max-h-[min(22rem,…)]`).
3. Hold (or repeatedly press) the **ArrowDown** key.

### Expected Behavior

The drawer scrolls so the highlighted row always stays visible while navigating with ArrowUp/ArrowDown — the standard behavior for autocomplete/combobox listboxes.

### Actual Behavior

The highlight index advances (wrapping at the ends), but the drawer's scroll position never follows. Once the highlight moves below the visible rows it is invisible; the drawer keeps showing the initial top rows. From the user's point of view the selection just disappears — a UX-observability bug.

### Affected Component

Other — **Desktop app** (`apps/desktop`, composer completion drawer)

### Debug Report

N/A — pure renderer-side UI bug in the desktop composer; no agent/gateway logs involved. Root cause identified in the source below.

### Operating System

macOS 15 (Darwin 25.5.0)

### Hermes Version

Hermes Desktop `apps/desktop` 0.17.0, repo `main` @ `d71033a40`

### Root Cause Analysis

The ArrowDown/ArrowUp handlers in `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/index.tsx` (~line 526) only update the active index:

```ts
if (event.key === 'ArrowDown') {
  event.preventDefault()
  triggerKeyConsumedRef.current = true
  setTriggerActive(idx => (idx + 1) % triggerItems.length)
  return
}
```

`ComposerTriggerPopover` (`apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/trigger-popover.tsx`) renders the rows inside the scrollable drawer (`overflow-y-auto` + `max-h` in `completion-drawer.tsx`), and marks the active row with `data-highlighted` — but nothing ever scrolls the highlighted row into view when `activeIndex` changes. There is no `scrollIntoView`/`scrollTop` logic anywhere in the trigger popover path.

### Proposed Fix

In `ComposerTriggerPopover`, scroll the highlighted row into view (`scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest' })`) whenever the active index changes via keyboard; pin the drawer to the top when the highlight wraps back to the first row (so the first group header stays visible); and skip scrolling for hover-driven highlight changes so the list never shifts under the pointer. PR incoming.

### Are you willing to submit a PR for this?

- [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: [Bug]: /diff crashes with UnicodeDecodeError on Windows when git output contains non-ASCII filenames or content

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
### What happens

`tools/working_diff.py` `_run()` calls `subprocess.run(..., text=True)` without an `encoding`, so git's output gets decoded with the platform locale. On a Japanese Windows machine that's cp932, and the moment the working tree contains a non-ASCII filename or diff content, `/diff` dies:

```
UnicodeDecodeError: 'cp932' codec can't decode byte 0xef in position 49: illegal multibyte sequence
```

Reproduced on a real Windows 11 machine (locale cp932) with an untracked file named `日本語ファイル.py`. Depending on the exact byte sequence the decode can also succeed as mojibake instead of raising, which corrupts the filenames in the diff output silently.

`_run`'s own docstring promises "Never raises on git failure", so callers don't guard against this.

### Why

git emits UTF-8 bytes for pathnames here (`_run` already passes `-c core.quotePath=false`), but the decode side is left to the locale. `tools/checkpoint_manager.py`'s `_run_git` hit the same problem and already pins `text=True, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace'` on every git call; `working_diff.py` just never got the same treatment.

### Fix

One line, matching the checkpoint_manager policy. PR incoming with regression tests (including one that pins the trade-off for legacy cp932-encoded blob content: lossy replacement characters, never an exception).

items.title: [Bug]: hermes gateway actions (start/stop/restart) hanging/extremely slow in Docker with volume binding after recent update

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
### Bug Description

Since the most recent update, executing hermes gateway start, hermes gateway stop, or hermes gateway restart inside a Docker container takes an abnormally long time to complete or hangs entirely. This behavior was never present in previous versions

The environment uses a mounted host volume bound to the Hermes home directory, which seems to hit an IO/lock synchronization bottleneck during process state transitions.

### Steps to Reproduce

Deploy Hermes Agent using a Docker container with a bound host volume (e.g., -v ~/.hermes:/root/.hermes).

Run hermes gateway start or hermes gateway restart.

Observe a multi-minute delay or timeout before the CLI acknowledges the action.

### Expected Behavior

Gateway lifestyle actions should resolve quickly (within seconds), releasing or establishing process locks cleanly without filesystem blocking

### Actual Behavior

The commands hang for an extended duration. Re-running the command shows that the gateway struggles to clear or verify the gateway.pid lock file over the active Docker volume binding

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp), Configuration (config.yaml, .env, hermes setup)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
Routing to the machine dashboard (profile 'robin' preselected). Use --isolated for a dedicated per-profile server.

→ gateway is now running under s6 supervision (auto-restart on crash,

  dashboard supervised alongside if HERMES_DASHBOARD is set).

  This is the recommended setup for the s6 container image — the

  gateway will keep running even if it crashes.

  Use `--no-supervise` (or HERMES_GATEWAY_NO_SUPERVISE=1) to opt out

  and get the pre-s6 foreground behavior instead.

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│           ⚕ Hermes Gateway Starting...                 │

├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤

│  Messaging platforms + cron scheduler                    │

│  Press Ctrl+C to stop                                   │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘


→ Using web dist from HERMES_WEB_DIST: /opt/hermes/hermes_cli/web_dist

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│           ⚕ Hermes Gateway Starting...                 │

├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤

│  Messaging platforms + cron scheduler                    │

│  Press Ctrl+C to stop                                   │

└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘


HERMES_DASHBOARD_READY port=9119

  Hermes Web UI → http://0.0.0.0:9119

WARNING gateway.run: No messaging platforms enabled.
```

### Operating System

items.title: MCP stdio: stale serve processes mask fixes + unbounded dart mcp-server accumulation (macOS)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Summary

Two compounding problems make MCP stdio servers (e.g. the bundled `dart mcp-server`) hard to diagnose and prone to silent resource leaks on macOS:

1. **Stale `serve` processes never pick up source fixes.** A `serve` worker imports `tools/mcp_tool.py` once at startup and keeps running for days/weeks. A code-level fix to logging or retry behavior does **not** take effect until every old `serve` is killed. This directly masks incident response: the `unhandled errors in a TaskGroup (N sub-exceptions)` unwrap fix (#65673) was already on disk, yet a `serve` started weeks earlier kept logging the *unwrapped* (masked) string for the entire interval.
2. **`dart mcp-server` subprocesses accumulate per idle session with no reaper / no upper bound.** Each `hermes_cli.main serve` spawns its own `mcp_stdio_watchdog.py` → `dart mcp-server`, and the child is launched with `start_new_session=True`. On macOS there is no `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG`, so an abandoned/idle session keeps its `dart mcp-server` alive indefinitely. Nothing caps the count or sweeps servers belonging to sessions that are alive but no longer used. Observed in the wild: **18+ concurrent `serve` processes, 37 `dart mcp-server` children, ~624 MB**, all with live Hermes parents — not orphans, just never reaped.

## Reproduction (observed on a real machine)

Environment:
- macOS, Hermes desktop app (`Hermes.app` → `hermes_cli.main serve`)
- MCP server config (from `~/.hermes/profiles/coder/config.yaml`):
  ```yaml
  mcp_servers:
    Dart-mcp:
      command: /Users/Shared/bin/flutter/bin/dart
      args:
        - mcp-server
  ```
- `dart` = Dart SDK 3.12.2; `mcp` Python SDK 1.26.0; `anyio` 4.12.1; Python 3.11.15

Steps / evidence:
1. `ps` shows 18 `hermes_cli.main serve` processes (started Jul 21 → Jul 27) and 37 `dart mcp-server` children, each parented to a live Hermes session.
2. `~/.hermes/logs/agent.log` shows `Dart-mcp` connection failures recurring every ~5 min from **2026-07-14** through the incident.
3. The emitted message is the raw masked string:
   ```
   WARNING tools.mcp_tool: MCP server 'Dart-mcp' failed initial connection after 3 attempts, parking until a reconnect is requested: unhandled errors in a TaskGroup (1 sub-exception)
   ```
4. Crucially, the **server binary is healthy**. Reproducing Hermes's exact spawn path succeeds every time:
   ```python
   # python3 mcp_stdio_watchdog.py --ppid <ppid> -- /Users/Shared/bin/flutter/bin/dart mcp-server
   # via mcp 1.26.0 stdio_client + ClientSession (anyio TaskGroup)
   initialize: OK  server=dart and flutter tooling v0.1.4
   tools/list: OK (13 tools); resources/list: OK (0); prompts/list: OK (1)
   ```
   This was verified across multiple cwds and both full and minimal env. The failure was **not** in `dart`, the protocol, or the environment — it was a function of the running `serve` process's stale state + the subprocess sprawl.

## Root cause analysis

### Finding 1 — stale module / no hot-reload of `serve`
- `_unwrap_exception_group` (tools/mcp_tool.py:973) and its log-site usage (lines ~3204, 3265–3271, 3295–3301) were added in commit `3e6b43776` ("fix(mcp): unwrap exception groups and park permanent failures immediately", #65673), dated 2026-07-26.
- `mcp_tool.py` on disk is dated 2026-07-27 and **correctly** unwraps: I exercised the helper against single-leaf, cancellation-sibling, nested, and all-cancellation exception groups — all flatten to a meaningful leaf (`BrokenPipeError`, etc.). A process running this code would **not** log the masked string.
- Yet the masked string appeared in logs through 2026-07-27. The only way: the emitting `serve` was started **before** the fix landed and never reloaded `mcp_tool`. Subsequent `hermes` restarts/relaunches spawned new `serve` workers, but old ones persisted (see Finding 2), so the pre-fix code kept running and logging.

### Finding 2 — unbounded `dart mcp-server` accumulation
- `tools/mcp_tool.py::_run_stdio` wraps the command in `mcp_stdio_watchdog.py` (start_new_session=True). The watchdog spawns `dart mcp-server` in its **own** process group and only forwards signals *downward* to its child. Nothing reaps *upward* when a session is abandoned.
- macOS has no kernel-level parent-death signal, so an idle session's `dart mcp-server` survives indefinitely. The `_kill_orphaned_mcp_children()` sweep (intended for truly orphaned children) does not fire for children whose *parent is still alive but unused*.
- Result: every unclosed/abandoned session pins a dormant `dart mcp-server`. Over a week of restarts this reached 37.

### Side note — the masked error itself
`unhandled errors in a TaskGroup (N sub-exceptions)` is anyio's `BaseExceptionGroup.__str__`. It is informative once unwrapped, but the *initial-connection* log path's behavior is only as good as the code the running process actually loaded — see Finding 1.

## Proposed fixes

1. **Reload/version-gate `serve` on config or source change.** At minimum, embed a source-hash or `__version__` in `mcp_tool` and have the supervisor (or the desktop app's process manager) restart `serve` workers when the loaded module's hash differs from on-disk. This makes "we fixed the logging" actually mean "the running process uses the fix." (Addresses Finding 1.)
2. **Cap and sweep idle MCP subprocesses.** For `start_new_session=True` stdio children, add a periodic sweep keyed on "session alive but no MCP activity for N minutes" → graceful `SIGTERM` to the child's process group, then `SIGKILL`. Also consider an upper bound on concurrent `dart mcp-server` (and MCP servers generally) per profile. (Addresses Finding 2.)
3. **Emit the unwrapped cause on the *parking* message too.** The `failed initial connection after N attempts, parking` warning (lines 3265–3271) already uses `type(root).__name__, root` after unwrap, so it's correct — but given Finding 1, ensure *all* `except Exception` paths in the reconnect loop call `_unwrap_exception_group` before logging, so a stale process can never again print the opaque string.

## Evidence artifacts
- `ps` inventory (18 `serve`, 37 `dart mcp-server`, live parents) — captured live.
- Standalone reproduction of Hermes's exact spawn + `mcp` 1.26.0 client handshake → success.
- Unit-style exercise of `_unwrap_exception_group` against 4 exception shapes → all flatten correctly.

## Severity
Medium (diagnostic opacity + slow memory/process leak on long-running desktop installs). Not a crash; degrades over days of uptime.

items.title: [Bug] Gateway _pending_messages.clear() discards unrecoverable messages on shutdown - FTS corruption data loss

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Summary

When FTS5 index corruption prevents `INSERT INTO messages`, the gateway accumulates messages in `_pending_messages` (disk=0, memory=N). On shutdown, `_finalize_shutdown_agents()` calls `self._pending_messages.clear()` — **discarding all pending data permanently**. The FTS corruption is already detected and logged, but the data is never preserved.

## Actual Damage (2026-07-27)

- Trigger: Bug #9 → EMERGENCY prune → 265 sessions bulk DELETE → FTS5 inverted index corruption
- Impact window: 19:54~20:14 KST (~20 minutes)
- `database disk image is malformed`: 68 occurrences in gateway log
- FTS write corruption warnings: 107 (disk=0, memory=N)
- Peak state: `disk=0, memory=33` — 33 messages existed only in gateway memory
- Result: gateway restart → `_pending_messages.clear()` → permanent loss
- Telegram session affected: minimum 15 messages lost

## Root Cause

**`gateway/run.py` line ~9793** — `GatewayRunner._stop_impl()`:

```python
self._pending_messages.clear()  # data loss: no persistence before clear
```

The detection code already exists at line ~21965 (`_select_cached_agent_history`):

```python
logger.warning(
    "Persisted transcript lagged live cached history for "
    "session %s (disk=%d, memory=%d); preserving live "
    "conversation context (possible FTS write corruption)",
    session_key, len(agent_history), len(_selected),
)
```

The gap: **detection works / preservation missing / clear() destroys**

Note: #71999 / #72001 address false-positives in this detection logic, but do NOT address data preservation.

## Why This Matters

Users experience "my conversation disappeared" with no recovery path:
1. FTS corruption goes undetected (integrity_check passes, FTS index is outside its scope)
2. Messages silently fail to persist
3. Gateway restart discards the only surviving copy (in-memory cache)
4. User reopens app → blank session → permanent data loss

## Proposed Fix

Two-phase approach implemented and verified on v0.19.0:

### Phase 1: Flush on shutdown

New file `gateway/shutdown_flush.py` (304 lines) + patch to `gateway/run.py`:

```python
# In _stop_impl(), BEFORE _pending_messages.clear():
try:
    from gateway.shutdown_flush import flush_pending_to_file
    flush_pending_to_file(self._pending_messages, reason="shutdown")
except Exception:
    pass
self._pending_messages.clear()
```

### Phase 2: Recover on startup

`recover_pending_to_db()` in `gateway/shutdown_flush.py` + startup hook in `gateway/run.py`:

```python
# After runner.start() success:
try:
    from gateway.shutdown_flush import recover_pending_to_db
    recovered = recover_pending_to_db()
    if recovered:
        logger.info("Recovered %d pending message(s) from shutdown flush", recovered)
except Exception:
    pass
```

Recovery behavior:
- Reads pending JSON files → INSERT into state.db directly
- Per-session isolation: one corrupt session doesn't block others
- Successful recovery: deletes flush file
- Failed recovery (FTS still corrupt): re-saves failed sessions to new flush file
- Empty pending: no-op, zero overhead

## Verification (all passed)

- Empty pending → no-op (no false positive)
- Flush → JSON file created with correct structure
- Recover → DB INSERT confirmed via COUNT(*)
- No pending files remain after successful recovery
- E2E: fake pending → gateway restart → DB recovery confirmed → file auto-deleted

## Files Changed

| File | Change | Lines |
|------|--------|------:|
| `gateway/shutdown_flush.py` | **New** | 304 |
| `gateway/run.py` | Patch (2 sites) | +20 |

## Related Issues

- #71999 / #72001 — cached-history guard false-positive (detection only)
- #68858 — v0.19 compaction + FTS bug (underlying cause)
- #68545 — state.db corruption on macOS virtiofs

## Full Design Document

See HanManager wiki: `wiki/system/hooks/2026-07-27_shutdown-memory-flush-hook-v1.md`

---

**Severity:** High — causes permanent user data loss with no recovery
**Reproducibility:** Triggered by any FTS corruption event (bulk DELETE, WAL corruption, etc.)
**Fix availability:** Working implementation attached; happy to open a PR.

items.title: Gateway sessions (Slack/Telegram/Discord) appear in Desktop general session list — should be excluded or configurable

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Problem

Gateway sessions from Slack, Telegram, and Discord appear in the Desktop app's general "工作階段" (Sessions) sidebar list alongside CLI/Desktop sessions. These sessions already have their own dedicated platform sections in the sidebar (e.g., "SLACK", "TELEGRAM"), so appearing in the general list is redundant and clutters the recents view.

## Current behavior

- Gateway sessions are stored in the same `state.db` with `source` set to `slack`, `telegram`, `discord`, etc.
- The Desktop sidebar API (`GET /api/sessions` and `/api/profiles/sessions/sidebar`) only excludes `cron` sessions by default (`exclude_sources=cron`)
- Gateway sessions with titles persist in the general list; unnamed ones (`title=NULL`) eventually disappear due to `include_unnamed=false` filtering
- This creates an inconsistent experience: Slack sessions flood the general list while their Telegram counterparts may be less visible due to lower volume

## Expected behavior

Gateway sessions should **not** appear in the general session list, because:

1. They already have dedicated platform sections in the sidebar with proper context (platform icon, thread mapping, user info)
2. The general session list is meant for local CLI/Desktop conversations
3. This is analogous to how `cron` sessions are already excluded by default

## Proposed solution

Same pattern as #57527 (which addressed cron sessions):

**Option A — Default exclusion (recommended):**
Extend the default `exclude_sources` to include gateway platforms:
```
exclude_sources = ["cron", "slack", "telegram", "discord", "bluebubbles", "matrix"]
```

**Option B — Configurable exclusion:**
Add a config option so users can choose:
```yaml
display:
  session_list_exclude_sources: "cron,slack,telegram,discord"
```

**Option C — `source` query parameter on the API:**
Already partially supported — make the Desktop sidebar pass it:
```
GET /api/sessions?source=desktop,cli
```

## Technical context

- `web_server.py` line ~4850: `exclude_sources` is CSV-parsed and passed to `list_sessions_rich`
- Default is `exclude_sources=cron` for the recents slice
- `hermes_state.py` `list_sessions_rich` already supports `exclude_sources` parameter
- Session `source` values: `desktop`, `cli`, `slack`, `telegram`, `discord`, `cron`, `bluebubbles`, `matrix`

## Related

- #57527 — filter out cron sessions from session listing (same pattern, different source)
- #70134 — archived-session management panel (mentions source splitting in sidebar)

items.title: [Feature]: Add Databricks as a first-class inference provider

labels.name: sweeper:not-planned
labels.description: Sweeper: closed per standing maintainer policy (design direction)

items.body:
## Problem or Use Case

Hermes can connect to Databricks Model Serving and Unity AI Gateway only through manual custom-provider configuration. This requires users to determine the correct endpoint, authentication method, model identifier, and wire protocol themselves.

Databricks provides governed access to models from multiple vendors and is a common inference layer for organizations that centralize model access. First-class support would make Hermes easier to deploy in those environments.

## Proposed Solution

Add Databricks as a first-class Hermes inference provider with:

- Setup through `hermes model` and `hermes setup`
- Databricks workspace URL and PAT/OAuth authentication
- Discovery and selection of available serving endpoints or model services
- Support for the appropriate Databricks inference interfaces, including Chat Completions and Responses where available
- Databricks-aware validation in `hermes doctor`
- Documentation for Model Serving and Unity AI Gateway

The implementation should use Hermes's existing provider and transport abstractions rather than adding a new model tool.

## Alternatives Considered

Custom providers work as a manual fallback, but they do not provide integrated authentication, model discovery, protocol selection, or setup validation.

## Feature Type

Inference provider integration

# Hermes Desktop App - Bug Report: SSH connection failure locks Settings dialog

**Title:** Desktop App: SSH auth failure makes Settings unreachable (window refreshes too fast, clicks ignored)

**Environment:**
- Hermes Agent Desktop App: v0.19 (built via `hermes desktop --build-only`)
- Windows 10 (German locale)
- Connection mode: SSH (`connection.json` mode=ssh)
- Hermes backend running locally on Lab:9119

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Configure Desktop App for SSH remote mode (Host 127.0.0.1, Port 22, User, private key, remotePort 9119) via `connection.json`.
2. Start the Desktop App (`Hermes.exe`).
3. If SSH authentication fails (e.g. wrong key path, Microsoft-account user, permission denied), the app shows: `SSH authentication to User@127.0.0.1 failed. Desktop runs ssh non-interactively...`
4. The app immediately retries / refreshes the connection window.
5. Try to click **Settings** (or the gear icon) to fix the connection config.
6. The Settings window does NOT open — the main window refreshes too fast and ignores the click.
7. Only the **Logfile** button responds; Settings is unreachable.

**Expected behavior:**
- On SSH connection failure, the app should allow opening Settings to fix the configuration (host/port/user/key/remotePort) without being locked out by a refresh loop.

**Actual behavior:**
- Settings dialog is unreachable after SSH auth failure; window refreshes and ignores clicks. User is stuck and must edit `connection.json` manually (`%APPDATA%\Hermes\connection.json`).

**Workaround (manual):**
- Edit `%APPDATA%\Hermes\connection.json` directly (mode ssh, remote.host/port/user/key/remotePort).
- Note: The app does NOT read `~/.ssh/config`; the private key must be referenced via the correct field in `connection.json`.

**Additional context:**
- Error from app: `kind: 'auth-failed'` with `originalError: Permission denied (publickey,password,keyboard-interactive)`.
- Root cause on Windows: OpenSSH Server (Win32-OpenSSH) does NOT support Microsoft-account users for shell/exec (`lookup_sid() failed`). A **local Windows account** must be used for SSH. The Desktop App should document this or surface a clearer error.

**Severity:** High (blocks configuration fix without manual file editing)

**Reported by:** Schrauberhirn (Discord: Schrauberhirn)
**Date:** 2026-07-27

items.title: [Bug]: [CRITICAL] Event Loop Stall (GIL) → WebSocket Disconnect → Renderer Reset → Destructive Bootstrap Recovery Loop

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
### Bug Description

## What Happened

The Hermes desktop disconnects from the backend every 30–60 seconds of active use and enters an infinite destructive bootstrap recovery loop. While chatting, the desktop UI freezes for **6–47 seconds**, then suddenly disconnects. The Electron main process says **"no Hermes install found"**, launches `hermes-setup.exe --update --branch main` (which reinstalls Hermes from scratch), kills itself, and forces a manual relaunch. After relaunch, the exact same cycle repeats immediately.

## 🔄 Persistence — This Bug Survives Everything

| Action | Result |
|--------|--------|
| ❌ Full Windows system reboot | Bug reappears within 1-3 conversation turns |
| ❌ Deleting all bootstrap markers, lock files, `desktop.log` | Same cycle |
| ❌ `hermes doctor --fix` (reported "no critical issues") | No change |
| ❌ Disabling Windows ASLR for Git Bash via `Set-ProcessMitration` | Still stalls |
| ❌ `hermes-setup.exe --update` (forced by the bug itself) | Replaces install but bug fires again immediately |
| ❌ Switching between different local models (my_combo, mimo) | Same GIL stalls |
| ❌ Removing HTTP_PROXY environment variables | Still disconnects |

**The bug is architectural** — it is in the single-threaded asyncio event loop and the Electron bootstrap recovery logic. No amount of config tweaking, cache-clearing, or reinstallation will fix it. Only code changes in `hermes_cli/web_server.py` and `electron-main.mjs` can resolve it.

## What Should Have Happened Instead

1. The event loop should never stall for >10 seconds, OR WebSocket heartbeats should be immune to GIL pressure (dedicated thread).
2. If the WebSocket drops, the renderer should **reconnect to the existing running backend** (which is still healthy) instead of entering bootstrap recovery.
3. `ensureRuntime()` should check the **active Hermes venv** (`...venv/Scripts/python.exe`) before falling through to system Python discovery.
4. A transient renderer disconnect must **NEVER** trigger `hermes-setup.exe --update` — that is a destructive reinstall, not a recovery mechanism.

## The Complete Failure Chain

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  BUG #1: GIL Pressure / Single-Threaded Design  │  ← ROOT CAUSE
│  Event loop stalls 6–47 seconds                 │
└──────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘
               ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  WebSocket heartbeat missed → Renderer drops     │
│  "ws send failed peer=127.0.0.1:XXXXX"          │
└──────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘
               ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Renderer requests "reset" to Electron main      │
└──────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘
               ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  BUG #2: Bootstrap Recovery on Renderer Disconnect│  ← COMPOUNDS THE BUG
│  Electron enters ensureRuntime() instead of WS   │
│  reconnecting to the still-running backend       │
└──────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘
               ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  "no Hermes install found" (FALSE POSITIVE)      │
│  → hermes-setup.exe --update                     │
│  → Desktop kills itself with                     │
│    "recovery handed off to Hermes Setup"         │
└──────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘
               ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  ♾️  INFINITE LOOP: User reopens desktop →       │
│  GIL strikes again → same cascade repeats        │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Steps to Reproduce

1. **Install Hermes desktop** on Windows via `git clone` + bootstrap. This creates a Python 3.11 venv at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\hermes-agent\venv\`.
2. **Configure a local model provider** — e.g., 9router at `localhost:20128`, or any local LLM inference server.
3. **Launch Hermes desktop** — the backend starts, the renderer connects to it via WebSocket, and the app appears usable.
4. **Use the chat** — send a message, then immediately send another one while the first response is still being generated. Or: run a tool that triggers CPU-heavy work (long file search, large code generation, rapid sequential API calls).
5. **Observe the freeze** — the desktop UI becomes completely unresponsive for 6–47 seconds. No input, no animation, no feedback.
6. **Watch the disconnect** — after the freeze resolves, the desktop either:
   - Shows a "reconnecting…" state briefly, then
   - The entire app quits, `hermes-setup.exe --update` launches, and
   - You must manually relaunch the desktop from the Start menu.
7. **Repeat steps 4–6** — this cycle repeats every 30–60 seconds of active use.
8. **Restart your computer fully** — reopen the desktop. The exact same cycle occurs immediately. This confirms it is **not a cache, config, or memory-leak issue** — it is architectural.

> ⚠️ **The bug reproduces WITHOUT any proxy.** HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY may amplify the stall durations (by adding network latency to model calls) but they are **not the root cause**. Users with any local model provider will hit this eventually.

### Attempted Fixes That Did NOT Help
- ❌ Full Windows system reboot
- ❌ Deleting `bootstrap-cache/`, all lock files, `.bootstrap*` markers, `desktop.log`
- ❌ `hermes doctor --fix` (reported "no critical issues")
- ❌ Disabling Windows Mandatory ASLR for Git Bash (`Set-ProcessMitigation -Disable ForceRelocateImages`)
- ❌ `hermes-setup.exe --update` forced by the bug itself (replaces install but same code)
- ❌ Switching between available models (`my_combo` → `mimo`)
- ❌ Removing proxy environment variables
- ❌ Upgrading embedded SQLite from 3.45.1 to 3.53.1 (via `hermes doctor`)



### Expected Behavior


1. **Event Loop Stability:** The backend event loop should remain responsive enough to send WebSocket heartbeats, even during CPU-heavy operations. If the GIL causes unavoidable stalls, the WebSocket heartbeat should run in a **separate thread** (via `loop.run_in_executor()`) so it is immune to event-loop blocking.

2. **WebSocket Reconnection:** When the renderer's WebSocket drops (for any reason), the renderer should attempt **automatic reconnection** to the existing backend — not jump to a full runtime validation cycle. The backend process is almost always still alive, healthy, and running.

3. **Runtime Detection Logic:** The `ensureRuntime()` function in `electron-main.mjs` should check the **existing Hermes venv** (`...hermes-agent\venv\Scripts\python.exe -c "import hermes_cli"`) BEFORE falling through to system Python discovery. The venv is used to launch the backend — it should be the first thing checked for recovery.

4. **No Destructive Recovery:** A transient renderer disconnect must **NEVER** trigger `hermes-setup.exe --update`. Updating/reinstalling is a user-initiated action, not an automatic recovery path for a network-level disconnect. At minimum, the app should log the disconnect and wait for the user to decide what to do.

5. **Graceful Degradation:** If the WebSocket cannot reconnect after N retries, the backend should stay running (serving CLI users) and the Electron app should show a "Connection lost — click to retry" screen rather than self-destructing.

### Actual Behavior


# BUG #1 — GIL Pressure Causes Event Loop Stalls, Breaking WebSocket

## Description

The Hermes backend runs on a **single-threaded `asyncio` event loop**. When CPU-intensive operations execute — specifically, model inference calls against a local LLM provider, heavy tool execution, or database I/O — they **hold the Python GIL and stall the event loop** for **6 to 47 seconds**.

During these stalls, the event loop cannot process any I/O, including WebSocket heartbeat frames. The renderer's WebSocket connection detects the missing heartbeats and disconnects.

## Raw Evidence from Logs

### GIL Stalls (105 occurrences in a single ~30-minute session)

```
WARNING hermes_cli.web_server: event loop stalled 6.1s (GIL pressure suspected)
WARNING hermes_cli.web_server: event loop stalled 8.1s (GIL pressure suspected)
WARNING hermes_cli.web_server: event loop stalled 12.1s (GIL pressure suspected)
WARNING hermes_cli.web_server: event loop stalled 12.4s (GIL pressure suspected)
WARNING hermes_cli.web_server: event loop stalled 21.8s (GIL pressure suspected)
WARNING hermes_cli.web_server: event loop stalled 39.4s (GIL pressure suspected)
WARNING hermes_cli.web_server: event loop stalled 47.0s (GIL pressure suspected)
```

> **Key observation:** The stalls range from **6.1s to 47.0s**. Even a 6-second stall is enough to break WebSocket heartbeats if they are configured with a short interval. The code already **detects** the GIL pressure (it logs the warning) but does **not mitigate** it.

### WebSocket Write Slow (frames queued during stall)

```
WARNING tui_gateway.ws: ws write slow (loop stalled >10.0s) peer=127.0.0.1:20607 — frame left in flight
WARNING tui_gateway.ws: ws write slow (loop stalled >10.0s) peer=127.0.0.1:20607 — frame left in flight
WARNING tui_gateway.ws: ws write slow (loop stalled >10.0s) peer=127.0.0.1:20607 — frame left in flight
WARNING tui_gateway.ws: ws write slow (loop stalled >10.0s) peer=127.0.0.1:20607 — frame left in flight
```

> Multiple frames are queued — the event loop cannot drain the WebSocket send buffer because it is blocked by the GIL-held operation. The `>10.0s` marker confirms the stall exceeds the WebSocket write timeout.

### WebSocket Disconnect (60+ occurrences)

```
WARNING tui_gateway.ws: ws send failed peer=127.0.0.1:50198 error_type=WebSocketDisconnect error=
ERROR    tui_gateway.ws: ws ready frame send failed peer=127.0.0.1:50198
WARNING tui_gateway.ws: ws send failed peer=127.0.0.1:29118 error_type=WebSocketDisconnect error=
ERROR    tui_gateway.ws: ws ready frame send failed peer=127.0.0.1:29118
```

> `error_type=WebSocketDisconnect` with **no error message** — the peer simply disappeared (TCP connection dropped). The `"ready frame send failed"` confirms the server couldn't deliver the readiness handshake because the peer was already gone.

### Root Cause Analysis (Bug #1)

```
Python asyncio event loop (single thread)
         │
         ├── [normal] sends WebSocket heartbeat → renderer stays connected
         │
         └── [stalled] LLM inference locks GIL for 6-47s
                      │
                      ├── WebSocket heartbeat never sent ❌
                      ├── Renderer's WS timeout fires
                      └── TCP connection drops
```

The fundamental issue: **Python's GIL + single-threaded asyncio** means CPU work blocks I/O. The WebSocket server and the LLM inference client share the same thread. Any long-running model call freezes the entire backend I/O, including the critical heartbeat that keeps the desktop renderer alive.

### Statistics from a ~30-minute Session

| Metric | Count |
|--------|-------|
| GIL stalls (`event loop stalled`) | **105** |
| WebSocket issues (`ws send failed` + `ws write slow` + `ws ready frame`) | **60** |
| Unique stall durations observed | 6.1s, 8.1s, 12.1s, 12.4s, 21.8s, 39.4s, 47.0s |


# BUG #2 — Renderer Disconnect Triggers Destructive Bootstrap Recovery Instead of Reconnection

## Description

When Bug #1 causes the renderer's WebSocket to drop, the renderer sends a **"reset"** request to the Electron main process. Instead of attempting to **reconnect the WebSocket to the existing running backend** (which is still alive and processing), the main process enters a full `ensureRuntime()` cycle.

`ensureRuntime()` checks whether `hermes_cli` is importable from the **system Python 3.13** — NOT from the Hermes venv where it's actually installed. Since the user's system Python is 3.11 (not 3.13) and does not have `hermes_cli` installed system-wide, the check fails with:

```
[hermes] Ignoring system Python ... hermes_cli is not importable; falling through to bootstrap.
[hermes] [bootstrap] no Hermes install found; starting first-launch bootstrap
```

It then launches `hermes-setup.exe --update --branch main`, which **downloads and reinstalls Hermes from scratch**, then kills the desktop with:

```
[hermes] [boot] Desktop boot failed: Hermes recovery was handed off to Hermes Setup.
```

The user is forced to manually relaunch the app, at which point Bug #1 fires again (GIL stall), and the entire cycle repeats **indefinitely**.

## Raw Evidence from Logs

### The Full Bootstrap Loop in `desktop.log`

```
[hermes] [boot] Hermes backend is ready. Finalizing desktop startup
[hermes] [tls] trusting 171 Windows system CA certificate(s) for backend connections
[hermes] [boot] Resolving Hermes backend
[hermes] [boot] Resolving Hermes runtime
[hermes] Ignoring system Python ... hermes_cli is not importable; falling through to bootstrap.
[hermes] [bootstrap] reset requested by renderer
[hermes] [bootstrap] no Hermes install found; starting first-launch bootstrap
[hermes] [updates] venv shim unlocked; safe to proceed
[hermes] [updates] Cached bootstrap installer file size: 174985 bytes
[hermes] [bootstrap] handed off bootstrap-needed recovery to updater: C:\Users\...\hermes-setup.exe --update --branch main
[hermes] [boot] Desktop boot failed: Hermes recovery was handed off to Hermes Setup.
[hermes] Ignoring stale Hermes backend exit (1)
```

⏳ *User reopens desktop… and the exact same log repeats:*

```
[hermes] [boot] Hermes backend is ready. Finalizing desktop startup
[hermes] [tls] trusting 171 Windows system CA certificate(s) for backend connections
[hermes] [boot] Resolving Hermes backend
[hermes] Ignoring system Python ... hermes_cli is not importable; falling through to bootstrap.
[hermes] [bootstrap] reset requested by renderer
[hermes] [bootstrap] no Hermes install found; starting first-launch bootstrap
[hermes] [bootstrap] handed off bootstrap-needed recovery to updater: hermes-setup.exe --update --branch main
[hermes] [boot] Desktop boot failed: Hermes recovery was handed off to Hermes Setup.
```

> **This exact sequence repeats every 30–60 seconds. Forever.** The user never gets more than ~60 seconds of desktop uptime.

### Key Timestamps (from `desktop.log`, lines ~1200–1415)

| Time | Event |
|------|-------|
| `20:52:28` | `[boot] Hermes backend is ready (HERMES_BACKEND_READY)` |
| `20:53:01` | TLS trust completed |
| `20:53:01` | `[bootstrap] reset requested by renderer` ← WebSocket dropped |
| `20:53:01` | `[bootstrap] no Hermes install found` |
| `20:53:01` | `handed off to hermes-setup.exe --update --branch main` |
| `20:53:02` | `Desktop boot failed: recovery handed off to Hermes Setup` |
| *user relaunches …* | |
| `20:54:31` | **backend ready again** (fresh process) |
| `20:55:04` | `[bootstrap] reset requested by renderer` ← WebSocket drops again |
| `20:55:04` | `no Hermes install found` |
| `20:55:04` | `handed off to hermes-setup.exe` |
| `20:55:05` | `Desktop boot failed` |

> Each loop cycle: backend starts → renderer connects → GIL stall (1–3 turns) → WS drops → bootstrap → reinstall → restart → repeat. Total cycle time: **~30–60 seconds per iteration**.

### Root Cause Analysis (Bug #2)

```
Renderer WebSocket drops (due to Bug #1)
         │
         ├── SHOULD DO: WebSocket reconnect to running backend (takes ~100ms)
         │             Backend process is alive and healthy.
         │
         └── ACTUALLY DOES:
                    │
                    ├── Renderer sends "reset" to Electron main process
                    │
                    ├── Electron main enters ensureRuntime()
                    │   → Checks system Python 3.13 for hermes_cli
                    │   → User has system Python 3.11 → check FAILS
                    │   → Ignores the perfectly good venv at
                    │     ...\hermes-agent\venv\Scripts\python.exe
                    │
                    ├── Falls through to bootstrap recovery
                    │
                    └── Launches hermes-setup.exe --update
                        → Replaces entire installation
                        → Kills the running backend (which was fine!)
                        → User must restart
```

Two distinct logical errors:

1. **`ensureRuntime()` checks system Python, NOT the existing venv** — Even though Hermes is installed and running from a venv at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\hermes-agent\venv\`, the runtime check intentionally ignores it and probes `python3.13`/`python3` on the system PATH. If those don't have `hermes_cli` importable, it concludes "not installed" and enters recovery. The working venv is never consulted.

2. **Renderer disconnect should not trigger `ensureRuntime()` at all** — The backend process is still running, the database files are still open, the model is still loaded in memory. A WebSocket reconnect would restore full functionality in under 100ms. Instead, the app enters a destructive recovery path that replaces the installation and kills the perfectly healthy backend.

```shell
### desktop.log — Complete Bootstrap Loop (3 consecutive iterations)


[20:52:28] [hermes] [boot] Hermes backend is ready. Finalizing desktop startup
[20:53:01] [hermes] [tls] trusting 171 Windows system CA certificate(s) for backend connections
[20:53:01] [hermes] [boot] Resolving Hermes backend

-- [user relaunches] --
[20:54:31] [hermes] [boot] Hermes backend is ready. Finalizing desktop startup

[20:55:04] [hermes] [bootstrap] reset requested by renderer

-- [user relaunches] --

[20:57:06] [hermes] [bootstrap] reset requested by renderer

[20:57:06] [hermes] [bootstrap] handed off bootstrap-needed recovery to updater: hermes-setup.exe --update --branch main
[20:57:07] [hermes] [boot] Desktop boot failed: Hermes recovery was handed off to Hermes Setup.


### errors.log — MCP Discovery Crash (related secondary crash)


ValueError: signal only works in main thread of the main interpreter
  File "tui_gateway\entry.py", line 190, in _run_mcp_server_discovery
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, _log_signal)


This crash occurs in an MCP discovery thread. `signal.signal()` is called from a non-main thread, which Python explicitly forbids. This means **all MCP servers** (git, puppeteer, windows-control, etc.) fail to load during every session, but they are retried every 30s, wasting CPU cycles.

### All Log Counts (Full Session Summary)

| Log File | Lines | Key Signals |
|----------|-------|-------------|
| `agent.log` | 34,249 | 105× GIL stall, 60× WS failure, 319× model context length probe |
| `desktop.log` | ~1,500 | 4× full bootstrap loop sequences |
| `errors.log` | 276 | 4× MCP signal crash, 15× `ResourceExhausted` from 9router |
| `gateway-exit-diag.log` | — | Gateway restart diagnostics |
| `mcp-stderr.log` | — | MCP subprocess stderr |
```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)


The issue comprises **two distinct, compounding bugs** — neither can be fixed by config changes or reinstalls.

### Root Cause — Bug #1 (GIL Pressure, `hermes_cli/web_server.py`)

The Hermes backend runs a **single-threaded `asyncio` event loop**. Python's GIL (Global Interpreter Lock) ensures only one thread executes Python bytecode at any time. When the event loop calls `await` on a CPU-bound operation (model inference via HTTP to a local provider, heavy tool executions such as `search_files`, `read_file`, large output processing), it blocks the event loop from processing any I/O — including WebSocket heartbeat frames.

**The code explicitly detects this condition** (`"event loop stalled X.Xs (GIL pressure suspected)"`) but does **not take any action to prevent it**. The warning is purely diagnostic — no workaround or mitigation is applied.

**File involved:** `hermes_cli/web_server.py` — the event loop monitoring code.

### Root Cause — Bug #2 (Bootstrap Recovery, `electron-main.mjs`)

When the renderer's WebSocket drops due to Bug #1, the Electron main process calls `ensureRuntime()` which probes system Python for `hermes_cli` instead of:

1. Checking the actual venv that launched the backend (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes\hermes-agent\venv\Scripts\python.exe`), OR
2. Simply reconnecting the WebSocket to the still-running backend

The system Python check fails (Hermes is installed in a venv, not system-wide), producing a false "not installed" result. This triggers `hermes-setup.exe --update --branch main`, a destructive reinstall that kills the healthy backend and forces a manual restart.

**File involved:** `electron-main.mjs` — `ensureRuntime()` function.

### Compounding Effect

Bug #1 causes the WebSocket to drop. Bug #2 responds to the WebSocket drop with destruction instead of reconnection. Together, they create an inescapable loop that makes the desktop entirely unusable and wastes the user's time with repeated reinstalls that never address the root cause.

### Bonus Crash — MCP Discovery (`tui_gateway/entry.py:190`)

During each desktop session, the MCP discovery thread calls `signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, _log_signal)` from a non-main thread. Python raises `ValueError: signal only works in main thread of the main interpreter`. This prevents **all** MCP servers (git, puppeteer, windows-control, mermaid, vega-lite, etc.) from loading. While not the primary desktop freeze issue, this crash wastes CPU on 30-second retry cycles and prevents any MCP tools from working.



### Proposed Fix (optional)

_No response_

Hey, this is a test of the hermes bug report skill. 


# [SKILLTEST] Discord cron delivery fails with 404 "Unknown Channel" when DISCORD_HOME_CHANNEL_THREAD_ID points to a deleted thread

> **[SKILLTEST]** — This issue is a deliberate end-to-end test of the `hermes-bug-feature-reporting` skill pipeline (V1 self-evidence → V2 GitHub dup-check → Stage 2 file). Root cause was a local `.env` misconfiguration, not a Hermes code defect. Filed as requested to exercise the workflow; safe to close as `not planned` / `invalid`.

## Bug Description
A scheduled cron job with `deliver: discord:<channel-id>` fails every run with a `404 Not Found (error code: 10003): Unknown Channel` error from the live Discord adapter, even though the configured `deliver` channel ID is valid.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Set `DISCORD_HOME_CHANNEL_THREAD_ID=<id-of-a-deleted-or-archived-thread>` in the profile `.env`.
2. Configure any cron job with `deliver: discord:<valid-channel-id>`.
3. Let the cron job fire (or run it manually).
4. → Delivery fails with `live adapter send failed: 404 Not Found (error code: 10003): Unknown Channel; live adapter delivery to discord:<dead-thread-id> failed`.

## Expected Behavior
Discord delivery to the configured `deliver` channel should succeed. A stale/dead `DISCORD_HOME_CHANNEL_THREAD_ID` should not silently break all outbound delivery, or at minimum Hermes should warn on gateway connect that the thread ID no longer resolves.

## Actual Behavior
The live adapter sends to BOTH the cron `deliver` target AND the `DISCORD_HOME_CHANNEL_THREAD_ID` target. When the thread ID points to a deleted/archived thread, the adapter throws `404 Unknown Channel`, and the entire delivery attempt is marked failed — even though the actual `deliver` channel was valid.

Observed error (verbatim from cron `last_delivery_error`):
```
live adapter send failed: 404 Not Found (error code: 10003): Unknown Channel;
live adapter delivery to discord:1527243910336876624 failed: 404 Not Found
(error code: 10003): Unknown Channel; delivery error: Discord API error (404):
{"message": "Unknown Channel", "code": 10003}
```

## Root Cause (local config, resolved)
`DISCORD_HOME_CHANNEL_THREAD_ID=1527243910336876624` in `profiles/werkstatt/.env` referenced a deleted thread. Fix applied locally: cleared the thread ID (`DISCORD_HOME_CHANNEL_THREAD_ID=`), kept `DISCORD_HOME_CHANNEL=1527236743621906482` (#hermes-talk, valid), restarted the gateway. Delivery then succeeded.

## Suggested Hermes-side improvement (optional)
Validate `DISCORD_HOME_CHANNEL_THREAD_ID` on gateway connect (resolve the thread via the Discord API); if it returns `Unknown Channel`, log a clear warning and skip home-thread delivery instead of letting it poison all outbound delivery.

## Environment
- Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20, upstream 8eaaa502), install: git
- Windows 11 25H2 (Build 26200, x64)
- PowerShell 7.6.4; OpenSSH Client 10.0.0.0
- Platform: cli (Werkstatt profile); Discord gateway bound to #hermes-talk
- Provider/model: nous / tencent-hy3-free

## Debug share (public, 6h auto-delete at time of test)
- Report:      https://paste.rs/Atb1u
- agent.log:   https://dpaste.com/DLXWJ8RUN
- gateway.log: https://dpaste.com/EUKQW7R3T
- gui.log:     https://dpaste.com/BTZZRU43Q

## Verification done before filing (Skill V2)
- `gh search issues` for `lookup_sid`, `exec request failed`, `Desktop SSH Permission denied`, `channel 0 ssh` → no matching Hermes issue for this specific symptom.
- Related (different failure): #50707 (ControlMaster on native Windows OpenSSH), #61557 (uv spawn / WinError 448 on Windows OpenSSH Server), #72700 (Desktop App SSH auth failure — separate, already filed).
- No duplicate of THIS Discord-delivery symptom found.

**[SKILLTEST END]**

items.body:
# [Bug] Provider 400 errors abort the agent instead of falling back to the next model in the chain

## Summary

When the configured main model returns a non-retryable HTTP 400 (param-shape mismatch, tool-message deserialization failure, etc.), the gateway **burns all 10 retry attempts on the same broken model** and surfaces a generic "model provider failed after retries" message to the user. The configured fallback chain (`model.default` + providers under each provider) is never consulted for 400-class failures.

This is reproducible across two different models in a single session — Xiaomi mimo-v2.5 via opencode-go, and MiniMax m3 via nvidia — both die on different 400s, and both fail the same way: no fallback, opaque user-facing error.

## Reproduction

1. Set `model.default = mimo-v2.5` (opencode-go) and run any moderately long agentic session. The gateway will eventually emit:

   ```
   ERROR agent.conversation_loop: Non-retryable client error:
     Error code: 400 - {'error': {'code': '400', 'message': 'Error from provider (Xiaomi): Param Incorrect', 'param': '`text` is not set', 'type': ''}}
   ```

2. Switch `model.default = minimaxai/minimax-m3` (nvidia) and run the same shape of session. The gateway emits the same shape of error from a different model:

   ```
   ERROR agent.conversation_loop: Non-retryable client error:
     Error code: 400 - {'message': 'Failed to deserialize the JSON body into the target type:
       data did not match any variant of untagged enum ChatCompletionRequestToolMessageContent
       at line 1 column 509697', 'type': 'Bad Request', 'code': 400}
   ```

3. The user sees only:
   ```
   ⚠️ The model provider failed after retries. I kept raw provider details out of chat; check gateway logs for diagnostics.
   ```

   The model is identified by handle ("the model provider"), not by name. Logs hold the real model+provider but the gateway intentionally scrubs that from the user-facing message.

## Evidence (from `~/.hermes/logs/errors.log` on a single potato host, 2026-07-27 session)

| Time (UTC) | Model | Provider | Error | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 13:06:36 | mimo-v2.5 | opencode-go | `429 Too many requests` (Xiaomi) | Retry 1/10 with backoff — recovers |
| 14:21:15 | mimo-v2.5 | opencode-go | `400` `param: 'text' is not set` | **Non-retryable, aborts conversation** |
| 14:23:58 | mimo-v2.5 | opencode-go | `400` `param: 'text' is not set` (repeat) | **Same abort** |
| 14:30:00 | minimaxai/minimax-m3 | nvidia | `400` tool-message content deserialize fail | **Same abort** |
| 15:03:51–15:07:52 | minimaxai/minimax-m3 | nvidia | Repeated `429 Too Many Requests` | 4 retry attempts w/ backoff, then aborts |
| 15:14:21 | minimaxai/minimax-m3 | nvidia | `400` tool-message content deserialize fail | **Same abort** |
| 15:22:38 | minimaxai/minimax-m3 | nvidia | `400` tool-message content deserialize fail | **Same abort** |
| 15:24:01–15:24:32 | minimaxai/minimax-m3 | nvidia | `429` | Retrying |

The pattern is unmistakable: **both models eventually hit a 400 on long conversations with accumulated tool-message history, and neither gets a fallback.** The user has to `/new`, edit `~/.hermes/config.yaml` to point at a different provider, and start over.

## Why this is a bug, not a feature

The retry policy already in place (`policy=default` in `agent.conversation_loop`) handles transient 429s and 5xx correctly — those *should* retry. The bug is what happens on:

- **HTTP 400 with a malformed-request shape** (the model API rejected the prompt structure) — retried 10x against the same broken model before giving up.
- **No provider-level fallback**: even when the config lists multiple providers (NVIDIA, Groq, OpenRouter all in `~/.hermes/.env`), a 400-class failure on `default` does not try the next one.
- **Opaque user message**: "the model provider failed" doesn't name the model or say what to do next. The user can't act on it without reading gateway logs.

## Expected behavior

When the configured `default` model returns a non-retryable 400 (param/deserialize class), the gateway should:

1. **Fall back** to the next model in the configured chain (e.g. if `mimo-v2.5` fails, try `groq/llama-3.3-70b-versatile`).
2. **Tell the user which model was abandoned and which it fell back to** — so they know to update `config.yaml` if they want to permanently switch.
3. **Only retry-against-same-model when the failure is transient** (429, 5xx, network) — the policy already does this. The gap is fallback, not retry.

## Suggested fix

In `agent/conversation_loop.py` (or whichever module owns the retry policy), extend the policy to handle 400-class failures with a fallback step:

```python
# Pseudo-code, exact location TBD
NON_RETRYABLE_400 = {BadRequestError, ...}

if error_type in NON_RETRYABLE_400:
    next_model = next_in_chain(current_model, config.providers)
    if next_model:
        log.warning(f"Model {current_model} returned non-retryable 400 ({e}); falling back to {next_model}")
        send_to_user(f"⚠️ {current_model} rejected the request shape; switching to {next_model} for the next turn.")
        return retry_with_model(next_model)
    else:
        # Truly stuck — surface a useful message
        send_to_user(f"⚠️ {current_model} rejected the request ({e.short_message()}) and no fallback is configured. See gateway logs.")
        abort()
```

The fallback list could live in `config.yaml` under `model.fallback_chain` (e.g. `["groq/llama-3.3-70b-versatile", "openrouter/nemotron-3-ultra-550b:free"]`).

## Environment

- Hermes version: as of 2026-07-27 (current)
- Host: `potato` (HP ProDesk, Ubuntu), Hermes user `datthemaster`
- Providers tried in this session: opencode-go (Xiaomi mimo), nvidia (MiniMax m3)
- Providers available but NOT tried automatically: groq, openrouter (configured in `.hermes/.env`, used for aux models)

## Severity

Medium. Doesn't corrupt data, doesn't leak secrets, but it bricks the user's session for an arbitrary amount of time on a model the user can't see and doesn't know how to switch away from in-flight. A retry-and-fallback chain makes the failure invisible; the current behavior makes it a 5-minute debugging detour.

## Workaround (for anyone hitting this now)

Edit `~/.hermes/config.yaml` to set `model.default` to a model with proven long-conversation stability (in this session: `groq/llama-3.3-70b-versatile` was used as the compression model all day and never 400'd). Restart the gateway. The agent picks up on the new model on the next message.
