items.body: ### Bug Description PR #72235 added Ctrl+F find-in-page to Hermes Desktop, but the find bar has two UX issues: 1. **Overlaps titlebar icons:** The bar sits at `fixed right-4` (1rem from viewport edge), directly competing for space with the titlebar system tools (layout, haptics, keybinds, settings gear, right-sidebar toggle) which render at z-70 above it. The icons visually float on top of the search bar, creating dead-click zones and obscuring the input. 2. **Appears behind full-screen overlays:** Pressing Ctrl+F while a full-screen overlay (Settings, Command Center, Agents, etc.) is open opens the find bar behind the overlay at z-50, where it's invisible but functionally active. When the overlay closes, the bar disappears — inconsistent behavior. This will also collide with the upcoming Settings search bar (#69025). ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Open Hermes Desktop 2. Press Ctrl+F (or Cmd+F) — observe the find bar overlaps the titlebar icons in the top-right 3. Close the find bar (Esc) 4. Open Settings (gear icon in titlebar) 5. Press Ctrl+F again — observe the find bar appears behind the Settings overlay (visible in the blurred background) 6. Close Settings via the X button — observe the find bar disappears ### Expected Behavior 1. The find bar should sit to the left of the titlebar tool cluster, not overlapping it 2. The find bar should not render on full-screen overlay routes (matching the titlebar controls pattern) ### Actual Behavior 1. Find bar overlaps titlebar icons, which float on top at a higher z-index 2. Find bar renders behind overlays, invisible but active; disappears when overlay closes ### Affected Component Other — Desktop app (Electron renderer) ### Debug Report N/A — this is a renderer-level UI layout issue, not a backend bug. ### Operating System macOS 26.5.2 ### Root Cause Analysis 1. `find-bar.tsx` line 162 uses `fixed right-4` — a static 1rem offset from the viewport edge with no awareness of the titlebar tool cluster at `right-(--titlebar-tools-right)`. 2. `find-bar.tsx` has no guard for overlay routes. The `isOverlayView()` check that `titlebar-controls.tsx` uses (line 217) to hide itself on overlays was not replicated in the find bar. Additionally, the keybind handler in `use-keybinds.ts` line 199 dispatches `openFindBar` unconditionally. ### Proposed Fix PR #72959 addresses both issues. Three changes in 3 files: - `find-bar.tsx`: Replace `right-4` with `right-[calc(var(--titlebar-tools-right,0.75rem)+var(--titlebar-tools-width,0px)+0.5rem)]` using existing CSS vars from wiring.tsx. Add `isOverlayView(appViewForPath(pathname))` guard. - `use-keybinds.ts`: Gate `view.findInPage` keybind on overlay routes so Ctrl+F is a no-op on overlays. - `find-bar.test.tsx`: Add regression test asserting find bar does not render on `/settings`. ### Are you willing to submit a PR for this? - [x] I'd like to fix this myself and submit a PR

items.title: Windows startup slow: optional skill provenance backfill repeatedly scans active skills

labels.name: duplicate
labels.description: This issue or pull request already exists

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Summary

On Windows, Hermes CLI startup can spend several seconds in bundled skill sync even when all bundled skills are already unchanged. The slow path is not the bundled skill hashing itself; it is the optional-skill provenance backfill repeatedly scanning the active skills tree.

In one local installation, this made every `hermes` launch feel blocked before the chat opened.

## Environment

- OS: Windows
- Hermes Agent: v0.19.0 (2026.7.20)
- Install method: git
- Python managed by Hermes: 3.11.15
- Bundled skills tracked: 69

`hermes --version` reports:

```text
Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20) · upstream 7c532e10 · local d71033a4 (+1 carried commit)
```

## Observed behavior

Starting Hermes calls:

```text
_sync_bundled_skills_for_startup()
→ sync_skills(quiet=True)
→ _backfill_optional_provenance(quiet=True)
```

The initial symptom looked like a hang in skill sync. After instrumentation, the repeated work was isolated to optional provenance backfill.

Measured before the local patch:

```text
_backfill_optional_provenance(quiet=True): ~5.685s
sync_skills(quiet=True):                 ~7.008s
```

The sync result was otherwise unchanged/no-op:

```json
{
  "copied": 0,
  "updated": 0,
  "skipped": 69,
  "user_modified": 0,
  "cleaned": 0,
  "suppressed": 0,
  "relocated": 0,
  "total_bundled": 69,
  "optional_provenance_backfilled": 0,
  "shadowed_by_external": 0
}
```

Direct hashing of the bundled source/target skill dirs was fast; the expensive part was the fallback lookup inside optional provenance backfill.

## Root cause

`tools/skills_sync.py::_backfill_optional_provenance()` iterates optional skills. When the canonical destination path is not present, it calls `_find_installed_skill_dir_by_name(src.name)`.

That helper performs:

```python
for skill_md in SKILLS_DIR.rglob("SKILL.md"):
    ...
```

Because it is called inside the optional-skill loop, the active skills tree can be recursively scanned many times during every CLI startup. On Windows machines with endpoint security/EDR, repeated small-file tree scans are noticeably expensive.

## Local patch tested

A minimal local patch indexes active skill directories by folder name once and reuses that index for the optional backfill fallback.

```diff
diff --git a/tools/skills_sync.py b/tools/skills_sync.py
index 288aa2dac..d213abe71 100644
--- a/tools/skills_sync.py
+++ b/tools/skills_sync.py
@@ -440,6 +440,37 @@ def _find_installed_skill_dir_by_name(skill_dir_name: str) -> Optional[Path]:
     return matches[0]
 
 
+def _index_active_skill_dirs_by_folder_name() -> Dict[str, List[Path]]:
+    """Index installed skill directories by folder name for optional backfill."""
+    index: Dict[str, List[Path]] = {}
+    if not SKILLS_DIR.exists():
+        return index
+
+    skills_root = SKILLS_DIR.resolve()
+    for skill_md in SKILLS_DIR.rglob("SKILL.md"):
+        if is_excluded_skill_path(skill_md):
+            continue
+        candidate = skill_md.parent
+        try:
+            candidate.resolve().relative_to(skills_root)
+        except (OSError, ValueError):
+            continue
+        index.setdefault(candidate.name, []).append(candidate)
+    return index
+
+
+def _unique_active_skill_dir_by_folder_name(
+    index: Dict[str, List[Path]], skill_dir_name: str
+) -> Optional[Path]:
+    """Return a unique installed skill directory from a precomputed index."""
+    if not skill_dir_name:
+        return None
+    matches = index.get(skill_dir_name, [])
+    if len(matches) != 1:
+        return None
+    return matches[0]
+
+
 def _backfill_optional_provenance(quiet: bool = False) -> List[str]:
@@ -467,6 +498,7 @@ def _backfill_optional_provenance(quiet: bool = False) -> List[str]:
 
     backfilled: List[str] = []
     changed = False
+    active_dirs_by_name: Optional[Dict[str, List[Path]]] = None
     for skill_md in sorted(optional_dir.rglob("SKILL.md")):
@@ -486,7 +518,9 @@ def _backfill_optional_provenance(quiet: bool = False) -> List[str]:
             # silently skips them forever. Fall back to a unique
             # same-directory-name match anywhere in the tree, then still
             # require a byte-identical hash below before claiming provenance.
-            dest = _find_installed_skill_dir_by_name(src.name)
+            if active_dirs_by_name is None:
+                active_dirs_by_name = _index_active_skill_dirs_by_folder_name()
+            dest = _unique_active_skill_dir_by_folder_name(active_dirs_by_name, src.name)
             if dest is None:
                 continue
```

## Results after local patch

```text
_backfill_optional_provenance(quiet=True): ~0.095s
sync_skills(quiet=True):                 ~0.564s
```

Validation after patch:

```text
python -m py_compile tools\skills_sync.py       OK
hermes config check                             OK
hermes -z "Responde apenas com OK."             OK
second hermes -z run                             OK
```

The sync result stayed the same: 69 bundled skills, all unchanged, no copied/updated skills.

## Expected behavior

A no-op startup sync should not recursively rescan the active skills tree once per optional skill. Optional provenance backfill should either:

1. pre-index the active skills tree once per sync, or
2. be skipped/cached when no provenance changes are possible, or
3. run only in install/update/repair flows rather than every CLI startup.

The local patch uses option 1 and preserves the existing byte-identical hash check before writing provenance.

## Notes

- This is a performance issue; no user skill contents were printed or modified during diagnosis.
- The patch does not disable bundled skill sync and does not bypass the existing provenance integrity check.
- This is likely more visible on Windows systems where endpoint security software adds overhead to repeated recursive filesystem scans.

items.title: Desktop GUI: prompt.submit sends to wrong session after session switch while model response is slow

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

items.body:
## Summary

When using Hermes Desktop GUI with multiple sessions open, user messages (``prompt.submit``) can be delivered to the **wrong session** after switching between sessions while one session's model response is still streaming. This leads to:

- Messages appearing in the wrong conversation
- "Ghost messages" that the user never typed appearing in the conversation
- Potential message loss when the intended session doesn't receive the input

## Observed Symptoms

1. **Message cross-talk between sessions** — text typed in session B appears in session A (or vice versa), confirmed by the user who saw the message appear in the wrong conversation history
2. **"Ghost messages" in conversation** — user saw messages they never typed appear as their own user messages in the conversation view (e.g. "继续", "继续完整回复问题")
3. **Database shows no record** — the ghost messages do NOT exist in the SQLite session store, confirming they are a frontend rendering artifact or a transient submission race

## Reproduction Conditions

The bug manifests under these concurrent conditions:

1. **Multiple sessions are active** in the Desktop GUI (tabs open in the sidebar)
2. **One session's model response is slow** (still streaming tokens, e.g. local llama.cpp at 127.0.0.1:8080, or a cloud model with high latency)
3. **User switches to another session** while the first session is still processing
4. **User types and sends a message** in the newly switched-to session

## Root Cause Analysis

### Backend (tui_gateway/server.py)

The ``prompt.submit`` JSON-RPC handler routes messages purely by ``session_id`` parameter:

```python
@method("prompt.submit")
def _(rid, params: dict) -> dict:
    sid = params.get("session_id", "")
    session, err = _sess_nowait(params, rid)
    ...
```

The backend has proper synchronization (``_sessions_lock``, ``_session_resume_lock``, ``history_lock``) and does not guess or auto-route sessions. **The backend is NOT the source of this bug.**

### Frontend (React/Electron/Ink UI — compiled in ``web_dist/``)

The most likely root cause is a **React stale closure or race condition** in the frontend's session state management:

1. The frontend maintains an ``activeSessionId`` state variable
2. When the user sends a message, ``prompt.submit`` is called with ``session_id: activeSessionId``
3. When the user switches sessions, the frontend updates ``activeSessionId`` via a state setter
4. If a model is slow (streaming), the WebSocket message queue may still be processing the previous session's tokens when the switch happens
5. The ``prompt.submit`` call captures a **stale** ``activeSessionId`` from a closed-over React state (a classic stale closure bug)
6. The message is delivered to the wrong session on the backend

**Additional evidence:** The "ghost messages" (words the user never typed appearing as user messages) also fit this pattern — the frontend may have submitted a placeholder, an auto-complete suggestion, or a prior session's draft text alongside the wrong ``session_id``.

### Why this wasn't seen on CLI

The CLI runs one session at a time. There is no session switching, no multi-tab state management, so the race condition never triggers.

## Environment

- **OS:** Windows 10, 64-bit
- **Hermes Desktop GUI** (not CLI, not gateway)
- **Backend model:** local llama.cpp (127.0.0.1:8080) + cloud models (deepseek, agnes)
- **Session source:** ``desktop``
- **Profile:** default profile

## Suggested Fix

**Frontend (UI layer):**
1. Guard ``prompt.submit`` against stale ``session_id`` by checking that the active session is still the intended target before sending
2. Add a monotonic counter to session activations — when the counter changes between when the user starts typing and when they submit, reject or re-route the message
3. Serialize ``prompt.submit`` calls per-session (queue rather than race)

**Backend (defense in depth):**
1. Add a ``session_id_version`` or ``expected_turn_id`` parameter to ``prompt.submit`` so the backend can detect stale submissions
2. Log a warning when a session receives a message while its streaming flag is set and the user is marked as "switched away" — this would help surface repro cases in logs

**Docs/UX:**
- Add a visual indicator when a session switch is still in progress (e.g. a brief "connecting..." state)
- Slow model responses should not block session switching UI state updates

items.title: Interrupt/abort silently no-ops when force_close_tcp_sockets() finds 0 sockets, leaving the request alive for minutes

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Summary

`_abort_request_openai_client()` can silently no-op: `force_close_tcp_sockets()` returns `0`, no `shutdown(SHUT_RDWR)` is issued, and the owning worker thread's blocked `recv` never unwinds. The interrupt logs success while the request stays alive on the wire for many minutes.

Against a self-hosted `llama-server` backend this leaks a server-side inference slot for the full duration of the abandoned request.

## Impact

Observed on a local llama.cpp deployment (`--parallel 2`, so two concurrent slots):

- User switched an interactive session to another model at `18:48:23`, request dispatched on `Thread-34`.
- User interrupted at `18:49:48` and switched back.
- The underlying stream did not close until `19:02:48` — **14 minutes later**.

During that window the backend accumulated 2 processing + 5–6 deferred requests, and average generation fell to ~0.7 tok/s. From the user's perspective the turn was cancelled; from the server's perspective it was still running. Because the abort logs normally, there is no signal that anything leaked.

## Evidence

```
18:48:34  OpenAI client created (chat_completion_stream_request, shared=False)
          thread=Thread-34 (_call)
18:49:48  OpenAI client aborted (stream_interrupt_abort, shared=False,
          tcp_force_closed=0, deferred_close=stranger_thread)
          thread=Thread-33 (run_agent)
18:49:48  Turn ended: reason=interrupted_during_api_call
19:02:48  OpenAI client closed (stream_request_complete...) thread=Thread-34
```

`tcp_force_closed=0` is the tell. Related, from the same session — the retry path fires while the prior attempt is still resident server-side:

```
Discarding chunk from superseded stream attempt 1 (discarded_chunks=1)
Stream drop on attempt 2/3 — retrying. error=RemoteProtocolError(stream attempt 1
was superseded) ... elapsed=977.84s ttfb=929.41s
```

## Analysis

The stranger-thread indirection introduced in `e51abb266` is **correct and should not be reverted** — routing a cross-thread close to `shutdown()` rather than `close()` is what prevents the FD-recycle corruption in #29507, where a released TLS FD was recycled into an unrelated `open()` and an unwinding SSL BIO wrote a TLS application-data record into a SQLite header.

The problem is that the abort's effectiveness is never checked. In `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py`:

- `force_close_tcp_sockets()` (~line 3506) increments `shutdown_count` once per socket yielded by `_iter_pool_sockets()`.
- `_iter_pool_sockets()` (~line 3242) walks `client._client → _transport → _pool → _connections`, then `conn._connection → _network_stream/_stream → _sock`.

When that traversal yields nothing, `force_close_tcp_sockets()` returns `0`, and `_abort_request_openai_client()` logs at INFO as though the abort succeeded. The worker keeps blocking until the server finishes on its own.

Notably, `chat_completion_helpers.py` (~lines 2536–2540) already documents a sibling case where `_abort_request_openai_client` is a known no-op on a singleton client with no per-request sockets, worked around for the MoA facade via `kind="stream"` (#57354). The failing path here appears to be a second instance of that class of mismatch — the client registered in `request_client_holder` not being the object that owns the live stream — though I have not confirmed which object is registered at abort time.

## What I ruled out

Tested against the installed versions below, driving real streaming requests and running the traversal from a stranger thread:

| Scenario | `_iter_pool_sockets()` | `force_close_tcp_sockets()` |
|---|---|---|
| Mid-stream (chunks flowing) | 1 socket | 1 |
| Pre-first-byte (long prefill, high TTFB) | 1 socket | 1 |

Traversal chain resolved fully in both: `SyncHttpxClientWrapper → HTTPTransport → ConnectionPool → HTTPConnection → HTTP11Connection → SyncStream._sock`.

So this is **not** a general httpx/httpcore version incompatibility, and **not** an artifact of blocking before the first byte. Both were plausible and both are dead. The zero-socket condition is specific to the failing call path.

## Suggested direction

Two changes seem worthwhile independent of the underlying cause:

1. **Make the failure visible.** `shutdown_count == 0` on an abort means the abort accomplished nothing — that deserves a WARNING, not an INFO logged identically to a successful abort. Silent failure is why this took a long incident to notice.
2. **Escalate when the abort is ineffective.** If no sockets were shut down, fall back to closing the stream/response object (as the `kind="stream"` path already does for the MoA facade), or mark the request cancelled so the retry loop does not re-dispatch on top of a still-live attempt.

Happy to test a patch against this deployment — the failure reproduces naturally under interrupt-heavy use with large contexts.

## Environment

- `httpx` 0.28.1, `httpcore` 1.0.9, `openai` 2.24.0
- Backend: self-hosted `llama-server` (llama.cpp) via LiteLLM proxy
- Introduced by `e51abb266` (2026-07-24), observed after merging `upstream/main` on 2026-07-26
- macOS host, Linux inference node

items.body:
### Summary

At commit `373632e33813c86b1b9b024168a5892af1926b83`, `hermes_cli/kanban_db.py::_inherit_notify_subs()` copies a parent task’s notification subscription to a child but omits the `chat_type` and `delivery_metadata` columns. The same omission remained on `main` when rechecked on 2026-07-27.

Subscriptions created by gateway `/kanban create` and tool-driven `kanban_create` can carry both fields. The explicit CLI subscription path can carry `chat_type`. `create_task(..., parents=...)`, `link_tasks()`, and `decompose_triage_task()` all call the inheritance helper, so inherited child rows silently lose available routing metadata.

### Impact

The recipient identifiers (`chat_id`, `user_id`, and `thread_id`) are preserved, so this is not a cross-recipient delivery issue. However:

- creator-wake reconstruction falls back to `chat_type="group"`, causing a DM-originated child completion to wake a fresh group-scoped session instead of the originating DM session;
- Telegram DM-topic subscriptions lose their persisted reply-fallback and topic metadata, while `message_thread_id` alone can render outside the intended visible lane.

### Reproduction

1. Add a parent notification subscription with `chat_type="dm"` and non-empty `delivery_metadata`.
2. Create a child with that parent, link an existing child with `link_tasks()`, or decompose a triage task.
3. Read the inherited child subscription.
4. `chat_type` and `delivery_metadata` are `NULL`, while the other routing fields are copied.

### Expected behavior

Inherited subscriptions preserve `chat_type` and `delivery_metadata`.

### Suggested fix

Include both columns in the helper’s `INSERT … SELECT`. Extend `_assert_inherited_notify_sub()` in `tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_notify.py` to assert them; the existing tests already exercise parent-linked creation, `link_tasks()`, and triage decomposition.

Related work: #56580, #60600, #72191, #72223, and #72232.

items.body:
## Summary

PR #72442 added `context-usage` to `STATUSBAR_HIDDEN_BY_DEFAULT` (commit 5b9518db4). This causes a deadlock: the item is hidden by default and cannot be recovered via the right-click toggle menu.

## Root Cause

The `context-usage` statusbar item has a **runtime** `hidden` condition:

```tsx
// apps/desktop/src/app/shell/hooks/use-statusbar-items.tsx:501
hidden: !contextUsage,
```

Where `contextUsage` comes from `usageContextLabel(currentUsage)`:

```tsx
// apps/desktop/src/lib/statusbar.tsx:43
export function usageContextLabel(usage: UsageStats): string {
  if (usage.context_max) {
    return `${compactNumber(usage.context_used ?? 0)}/${compactNumber(usage.context_max)}`
  }
  return usage.total > 0 ? `${compactNumber(usage.total)} tok` : 
}
```

`$currentUsage` is initialized without `context_max`/`context_used`/`context_percent`:

```tsx
// apps/desktop/src/store/session.ts:361
export const $currentUsage = atom<UsageStats>({
  calls: 0,
  input: 0,
  output: 0,
  total: 0
})
```

The only code path that populates `context_max`/`context_used` is `publishContextUsage` → `ContextUsagePanel.onUsageSnapshot`, which fires when **ContextUsagePanel fetches data from the backend**. But ContextUsagePanel only mounts when the user clicks the statusbar item — which is hidden because `contextUsage` is empty.

**Deadlock:** Item hidden → user toggles it on → runtime `hidden: !contextUsage` still true → item stays invisible → panel never mounts → context data never populated → item stays invisible forever.

## Items NOT affected

`running-timer` (`hidden: !busy || !turnStartedAt`) and `session-timer` (`hidden: !sessionStartedAt`) are **not** affected because their runtime data (`$busy`, `$turnStartedAt`, `$sessionStartedAt`) comes from independent backend events, not from clicking the item itself.

## Suggested fix

Remove `context-usage` from `STATUSBAR_HIDDEN_BY_DEFAULT` in `apps/desktop/src/store/statusbar-prefs.ts`, or alternatively populate `$currentUsage` with context data from an independent source (the periodic status poll) so the item can show once toggled on.

items.title: [ready-for-agent] Owner-specific, fail-closed cleanup gate for Luxiaonan WAV cache
items.body:
## Problem Statement

A disk-constrained cleanup workflow identified a large cache family of 101 WAV files (about 15 GiB) whose retained transcript segments are much smaller and are the artifacts currently referenced by downstream learning and evidence workflows. The user explicitly wants the unimportant, duplicative cache layer removed while preserving important evidence and avoiding speculative infrastructure.

The generic filesystem dependency preflight currently fails closed on these WAV files because their owner, consumer, and validator roles are unknown. A proposed generic relaxation was rejected after two independent, replayable counterexamples:

1. An unrelated JSON document with the expected hash could satisfy the proposed evidence shape.
2. A typed but self-attested document could still claim role resolution without proving a real owner, consumer, validator, or recovery path.

The relaxation was rolled back. The original validator and its original tests pass again, and the representative WAV correctly remains vetoed. The remaining problem is not “make the generic gate pass”; it is “add the smallest owner-specific proof that can safely decide this exact cache family.”

Recovery also cannot be described as byte-identical. Re-generated audio differed in file hash and decoded duration, and one current source video was materially longer than its historical WAV. The acceptable claim is therefore limited to operational recovery for the relevant downstream use, subject to an owner-specific test.

## Solution

Add one owner-specific, fail-closed cleanup validator for the Luxiaonan transcript WAV cache family and connect it to the existing highest-level cleanup preflight.

The validator should:

- Resolve the exact cleanup bundle before any mutation: the 101 intended WAV targets, their source-video identities, and their retained transcript-segment identities.
- Protect all transcript-segment artifacts and reject any cleanup bundle that includes them.
- Compute evidence directly from live files and known consumers instead of accepting free-text observations or self-attested PASS claims.
- Verify that retained transcript segments parse successfully and remain usable by the actual downstream consumer entry point.
- Check live file identity, graph coverage, fixed-path consumers/producers, unknown roles, and open handles.
- Distinguish byte-identical reconstruction from operational ASR-input reconstruction. The former is not required and must not be claimed; the latter must be proved by a real owner-specific consumer test.
- Detect source/WAV duration or content drift and either veto or explicitly downgrade the recovery claim according to a deterministic policy.
- Bind the receipt to the exact target set, exact live hashes, exact retained artifacts, exact authorization scope, validator version, and consumer-test result.
- Return a machine-verifiable PASS/VETO receipt that the existing cleanup preflight consumes.
- Keep the generic filesystem dependency graph as candidate evidence only. It must not grant deletion authority.
- Require a separate, explicit deletion execution after the validator and cleanup preflight pass. The implementation itself must not auto-delete files.

## User Stories

1. As a disk-constrained user, I want the validator to enumerate the exact WAV targets so that an estimate such as “about 15 GiB” corresponds to a reproducible file set.
2. As a disk-constrained user, I want transcript segments excluded and protected so that cleanup cannot remove the compact evidence I still need.
3. As a user, I want one high-level preflight entry point so that I do not have to interpret several unrelated reports manually.
4. As a user, I want the preflight to fail closed when evidence is incomplete so that low free space does not silently lower the safety standard.
5. As a user, I want the expected reclaimed space reported before deletion so that I can judge whether the cleanup is worthwhile.
6. As a user, I want live hashes bound into the receipt so that a later file change invalidates an earlier decision.
7. As a user, I want open handles checked so that an active transcription or playback process prevents cleanup.
8. As a user, I want fixed-path consumers and producers checked so that a live dependency cannot be mistaken for an unused cache.
9. As a user, I want unknown roles to remain a veto unless the owner-specific validator proves them so that generic uncertainty is never converted into safety.
10. As a user, I want arbitrary JSON documents rejected so that unrelated evidence cannot unlock deletion.
11. As a user, I want typed but self-attested claims rejected so that a document cannot validate itself merely by using the right field names.
12. As a user, I want real transcript parsing checked so that retained segments are not merely present but structurally usable.
13. As a user, I want the actual downstream consumer invoked on retained segments so that “still useful after cleanup” is behaviorally tested.
14. As a user, I want source-video mappings verified so that every cleanup target has a known provenance.
15. As a user, I want source/WAV drift detected so that current source files are not falsely described as exact replacements for historical WAVs.
16. As a user, I want operational reconstruction separated from byte-identical reconstruction so that the receipt makes only the claim the evidence supports.
17. As a user, I want regeneration commands or recipes bound to the owner-specific validator version so that recovery is reproducible and reviewable.
18. As a user, I want authorization bound to the exact file family so that approval to clean WAV cache cannot expand to transcripts, videos, workspaces, or unrelated caches.
19. As a user, I want an extra or missing target to veto the bundle so that partial enumeration and scope drift cannot pass.
20. As a user, I want the validator to produce durable PASS/VETO reasons so that another agent or human can replay the decision without relying on chat history.
21. As a reviewer, I want the two prior counterexamples preserved as regression tests so that the rejected generic relaxation cannot reappear under a different schema.
22. As a reviewer, I want the generic dependency validator left unchanged unless a separate generic design proves semantic ownership so that this local cleanup does not weaken all cleanup decisions.
23. As a reviewer, I want a single replayable counterexample to veto acceptance so that test counts cannot outvote a real safety failure.
24. As an operator, I want deletion to remain a separate explicit step so that a passing evidence gate cannot mutate the filesystem by itself.
25. As an operator, I want post-action verification of target absence, retained-segment integrity, downstream consumer behavior, and reclaimed free space so that completion reflects the actual machine state.
26. As an operator, I want failures to retain the files and produce the next exact evidence gap so that the workflow stops safely instead of inventing a workaround.
27. As a maintainer, I want the solution to reuse the existing dependency graph, scoreback format, and cleanup preflight so that it adds no parallel authority or second runtime.
28. As a maintainer, I want no daemon, watcher, hook, scheduler, or new database so that a one-time cleanup does not become permanent infrastructure.

## Implementation Decisions

- Implement an owner-specific validator rather than relaxing the generic unknown-role policy.
- Integrate at the existing cleanup-preflight seam; do not create a second cleanup authority.
- Treat all external manifests and receipts as candidate evidence until the validator recomputes and binds live identities.
- Use deterministic, typed output with explicit PASS/VETO reasons and a digest covering targets, retained artifacts, source identities, authorization, validator version, and consumer-test result.
- Make semantic role resolution depend on real owner-specific computations and behavior, not on a caller-provided role label or observation string.
- Model reconstruction capability with explicit claim levels. Byte-identical reconstruction is false for the observed data and must remain unavailable; operational reconstruction is allowed only when the owner-specific consumer test passes.
- Reject partial bundles, target drift, retained-artifact drift, source drift outside policy, open handles, live consumers, graph failures, unknown roles, and authorization mismatches.
- Keep deletion out of the validator. A PASS receipt is evidence for a separately authorized cleanup action, not permission to mutate files.
- Prefer the smallest implementation that reuses the existing validator and receipt contracts. Do not add a plugin, provider, service, or background runtime.
- Preserve the original generic validator behavior and add regressions that make the two rejected self-attestation designs impossible.

## Testing Decisions

Use one highest-level acceptance seam: run the owner-specific cleanup preflight on an exact target bundle and assert the resulting source-bound receipt.

Required acceptance and regression coverage:

- A valid minimal owner fixture with WAV targets, source identities, retained segments, no open handles, no consumers, matching authorization, and a passing downstream consumer test produces an evidence PASS but performs no deletion.
- An unrelated JSON document with the correct hash cannot resolve any owner, consumer, or validator role.
- A correctly shaped but self-attested role document cannot resolve roles without owner-specific computation and behavioral proof.
- A live incoming dependency vetoes the bundle.
- An open handle vetoes the bundle.
- Target-set additions, omissions, or order-independent digest drift veto the bundle.
- Live hash drift after inspection vetoes the bundle.
- Including a transcript-segment artifact in deletion targets vetoes the bundle.
- A missing or invalid retained segment vetoes the bundle.
- A failing downstream transcript consumer vetoes the bundle.
- A missing source mapping vetoes the bundle.
- A materially incompatible source/WAV duration or content mismatch vetoes operational recovery unless an explicit owner policy and consumer test support the downgraded claim.
- A byte-identical recovery claim always fails for non-identical regenerated output.
- An authorization scope that does not exactly cover the target family vetoes the bundle.
- Graph refresh, graph validation, coverage, open-handle, or identity errors remain fail-closed.
- A post-action scoreback verifies exact target absence, retained-segment integrity, downstream consumer behavior, and reclaimed space; it must not be generated by the validator itself.

Verification should run the narrow owner-specific test first, then the existing filesystem dependency graph suite, then the repository’s canonical test entry point for all touched code. Acceptance requires replaying both prior counterexamples against the final digest.

## Out of Scope

- Performing the actual WAV deletion as part of this implementation.
- Relaxing generic owner, consumer, validator, unknown-role, incoming-dependency, open-handle, or graph-coverage policy.
- Byte-identical reconstruction guarantees.
- Whole-machine cleanup, deduplication, or storage optimization.
- Modifying or deleting transcript segments, source videos, active learning workspaces, memory stores, dependency-graph state, or unrelated caches.
- Adding a daemon, watcher, hook, scheduler, background job, provider, plugin, database, or alternate runtime.
- Creating automatic deletion authority from a graph result, manifest, receipt, or test PASS.
- Refactoring adjacent cleanup, transcription, memory, or evidence workflows.

## Further Notes

- Observed cleanup candidate: 101 WAV files, approximately 15 GiB.
- Retained transcript segments are approximately 168 MiB and are the artifacts currently referenced by downstream code and evidence.
- The existing generic preflight correctly remains VETO after rollback because owner, consumer, and validator roles are unresolved.
- The original validator was restored to its prior digest and its original test suite passed after rollback.
- A full graph validation was manually stopped after several minutes, so no full-graph PASS is claimed.
- Regenerated audio differed in hash and decoded duration, and one current source video was approximately 24.7 minutes longer than its historical WAV. Recovery claims must remain operational and owner-tested, not byte-identical.
- The reusable governance rule is fail-closed: graph failures, stale or missing coverage, live identity drift, open handles, important unknowns, fixed-path consumers/producers, or one replayable counterexample are all vetoes.
- The earlier generic relaxation was deliberately rejected after two same-family counterexamples. The next implementation should stay owner-specific and stop if the same semantic self-attestation failure reappears.
- Requested tracker label: `ready-for-agent`. If the repository does not provide that label or the submitting account cannot apply labels, the issue title/body should preserve the requested readiness state and the exact label limitation should be reported.

Provide one deterministic owner-specific command that inspects the current Luxiaonan transcript cache without deleting anything and emits a source-bound receipt for the exact cleanup bundle.

items.title: [ready-for-agent] Verify future post-cleanup state and run live no-delete acceptance
items.body:
Parent: #73049

## Objective
Complete the verification seam around the owner-specific Luxiaonan WAV cleanup gate without deleting any live WAV in this ticket.

## What to build
- Add a post-action verifier that consumes the accepted preflight receipt plus a future post-action snapshot.
- Verify the exact approved WAV target set is absent, retained segment JSONL identities are unchanged, the retained-segment consumer behavior still passes, and reclaimed bytes match the approved bundle within the filesystem measurement contract.
- Run the owner validator and highest cleanup preflight against the current live cache in no-delete mode and persist a durable acceptance receipt.
- Replay the two historical self-attestation counterexamples so a correctly shaped or hash-matching caller document cannot unlock cleanup.

## Acceptance criteria
- The current live no-delete run freezes the exact 101 WAV / 101 retained segment pairing and reports the current candidate byte total; it performs no deletion.
- Every retained segment JSONL parses, every WAV maps to exactly one source media owner record, source media is decodable, and source duration covers the maximum retained segment end.
- The claim remains `OPERATIONAL_ASR_INPUT_RECONSTRUCTION_ONLY`; byte-identical reconstruction is explicitly rejected and the known duration/byte drift remains recorded.
- Open handles, identity drift, source ambiguity, segment drift, unapproved graph risks, or consumer failure remain VETO.
- Fixture acceptance proves the post-action verifier rejects partial deletion, missing retained segments, altered retained segments, consumer failure, and inconsistent reclaimed-byte accounting.
- Both self-attestation counterexamples are replayed through the highest cleanup entrypoint and remain VETO.
- Relevant repository tests, filesystem-dependency-graph tests, the real entrypoint smoke test, diff/hash review, and the canonical code-patch gate pass on the same changed-file digest.

## Out of scope
- Deleting the live WAV bundle.
- Relaxing cleanup policy for any other path or role.
- Daemons, watchers, hooks, background jobs, a new database, or automatic deletion authority.

## Blocked by
- #73056

## Done when
A future authorized cleanup can be verified end-to-end, while the current live run produces only evidence and no destructive action.

items.title: [Bug]: macOS Desktop — stuck white screen; remote OAuth expired / WS ticket loop + renderer crashes

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description

**P0 — macOS Hermes Desktop boots to a stuck white/blank screen with no usable UI text.** The app never finishes loading a working chat surface.

Desktop logs show a **remote-gateway OAuth session failure loop** as the primary failure, with secondary renderer crashes that blank the UI when reconnect thrashing races the assistant-ui store.

This is **not** the brief white flash on launch (#68640). It is a **stuck blank UI** until the remote connection is fixed outside the app (or the process is force-quit).

### Log signals (sanitized; hostnames redacted)

Repeating:

1. `Your remote gateway session has expired. Open Settings → Gateway and click "Sign in" again.`
2. `Remote Hermes gateway uses OAuth, but you are not signed in.`
3. `Could not reach the remote Hermes gateway while refreshing its WebSocket ticket.`

Secondary renderer:

4. `Composer is not available`
5. `useClientLookup: Index out of bounds` (same family as #61958 / `MessageRenderBoundary`)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Point Hermes Desktop (macOS) at a **remote** gateway with **OAuth** auth (Settings → Gateway → remote URL + OAuth session).
2. Let the OAuth access/session go stale (idle past cookie/token lifetime, remote dashboard restart, or clear partition/cookies while leaving mode = remote OAuth).
3. Cold-launch the Desktop app (or relaunch after update).
4. Observe the main window.

**Variant B — mid-session drop**

1. Boot successfully against remote OAuth.
2. Invalidate the remote session server-side (restart dashboard / revoke cookie) while Desktop is open.
3. Observe reconnect behavior and whether the shell stays usable.

## Expected Behavior

- App never stays on an empty white window with no chrome or recovery path.
- On confirmed remote OAuth rejection (`needsOauthLogin` / `isReauthRequired`), surface **`BootFailureOverlay`** immediately with:
  - the exact reauth copy,
  - **Sign in** (native OAuth / password shape as probed),
  - embedded **Gateway settings**,
  - **Use local gateway** escape hatch.
- Settings → Gateway remains reachable during auth failure.
- Transient `useClientLookup` / `Composer is not available` races must **not** blank the whole window (message-level boundary or root recovery, not full whiteout).
- Ticket mint / HTTP probe failures that are **transport** (timeout, 5xx) stay connectivity errors with retry; only **401/403 / tagged reauth** force Sign in.

## Actual Behavior

- Window stays **white / blank**, little or no readable UI.
- Logs loop on the three remote OAuth / WS-ticket messages above.
- Renderer also throws `Composer is not available` and `useClientLookup: Index out of bounds`.
- User cannot complete Sign in from a usable recovery surface; app feels hard-bricked until connection config is fixed externally.

## Affected Component

- Other → **Hermes Desktop (Electron) — macOS**
- Gateway connection / remote OAuth boot path
- Related: Messaging Platform N/A (CLI-only for template purposes)

## Debug Report

```shell
N/A for public filing — Desktop UI + local Electron logs only.
Reporter did not run `hermes debug share` (would risk private remote URL / host identity).
Sanitized log phrases above are the stable product strings.
```

## Operating System

macOS (Hermes Desktop)

## Python Version

N/A (Desktop shell)

## Hermes Version

Latest Desktop build as of report (post-update install). Please ask if a specific build number is required.

## Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell
Your remote gateway session has expired. Open Settings → Gateway and click "Sign in" again.
Remote Hermes gateway uses OAuth, but you are not signed in.
Could not reach the remote Hermes gateway while refreshing its WebSocket ticket.
Error: Composer is not available
Error: useClientLookup: Index out of bounds
```

## Root Cause Analysis (optional)

### Primary — remote OAuth ticket / session gate fails, recovery UI does not win the screen

Exact product strings live in the Desktop main process:

| Message | Location |
|--------|----------|
| `Your remote gateway session has expired…` | `apps/desktop/electron/backend-health.ts` — `REMOTE_SESSION_EXPIRED_MESSAGE` / `makeReauthRequiredError`; also `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts` gateway ticket failure path |
| `Remote Hermes gateway uses OAuth, but you are not signed in…` | `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts` (OAuth branch when `oauthSessionIsLive` fails and `oauthGuardMayHardFail`) |
| WS ticket refresh failure split | `apps/desktop/electron/main.ts` — `gatewayTicketFailure(…, expiredMsg, reachabilityMsg)` and `apps/desktop/electron/connection-config.ts` |

Boot / overlay ladder:

- `apps/desktop/src/app/gateway/hooks/use-gateway-boot.ts` — initial `getConnection` / `resolveGatewayWsUrl` / reconnect; reauth notifies via `isGatewayReauthRequired`; escalation to `failDesktopBoot` only after reconnect threshold.
- `apps/desktop/src/components/gateway-connecting-overlay.tsx` — fullscreen connecting when gateway not open and `!boot.error` during **initial** boot.
- `apps/desktop/src/components/boot-failure-overlay.tsx` — recovery **only** when `boot.error && !boot.running`.
- `apps/desktop/src/components/boot-failure-reauth.ts` — classifies remote reauth + Sign in copy.

**Failure class:** while remote OAuth is dead, the UI can sit in a state where:

1. connection never reaches `open`,
2. `boot.error` is null or not latched as confirmed reauth soon enough,
3. connecting/recovery paints poorly (white / empty) so the user never sees Sign in / Gateway settings,

matching the documented “dead-end CONNECTING combo” tests in:

- `apps/desktop/src/app/gateway/hooks/use-gateway-boot.test.tsx`
- `apps/desktop/src/components/gateway-connecting-overlay.test.tsx`

Also related open issues (cite, **do not** close as duplicate without matching **stuck white + these three log lines**):

- #68517 — basic-auth misclassified as OAuth / blank sign-in
- #61457 — remote cookie never persists
- #70572 — remote OAuth empty provider
- #68640 — brief flash white on open (different)
- #61958 — `tapClientLookup` out-of-bounds (secondary)

### Secondary — renderer races during reconnect thrash blank the shell

- `apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/message-render-boundary.tsx` — swallows **only** `useClientLookup|tapClient(Lookup|Resource).*out of bounds` inside a message boundary; if the throw escapes (root / composer tree / no boundary), whole UI whites out (#61958 family).
- `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/composer-text-guard.test.tsx` / edit composer paths — `Error: Composer is not available` when assistant-ui composer scope is missing during mount/reconnect.

## Proposed Fix (optional)

1. **Hard-latch confirmed remote OAuth rejection on cold boot** before any long CONNECTING spin:
   - If `getConnection` / `resolveGatewayWsUrl` / ticket mint returns `needsOauthLogin` or `isReauthRequired`, call `failDesktopBoot(message)` immediately and set the reauth latch used by `BootFailureOverlay` (see `apps/desktop/electron/backend-start-failure.ts` + main reauth latch comments around confirmed remote reauth).
2. **Never cover recovery with a blank shell:** connecting overlay must show branded copy + “Open Gateway settings” / “Sign in” even before `boot.error`; if auth-shaped, skip straight to `BootFailureOverlay`.
3. **Escape hatch always:** “Use local gateway” + open Gateway settings embedded panel must work without a live WS.
4. **Root error boundary** for assistant-ui lookup / composer-not-available: recover shell (sidebar + empty chat + recovery banner), not white window. Tighten `MessageRenderBoundary` coverage / ensure composer mount does not throw uncaught during boot.
5. Keep AGENTS.md auth ladder: only 401/403 / tagged auth = reauth; timeouts stay connectivity.

## Tests

- Extend `use-gateway-boot.test.tsx`: cold boot where `getConnection` rejects with `needsOauthLogin` → `boot.error` set, **no** indefinite connecting-only state.
- Extend `gateway-connecting-overlay.test.tsx` / `boot-failure-overlay.test.tsx`: OAuth expired strings → Sign in CTA visible; Settings / local fallback clickable.
- Extend `backend-health.test.ts` / `connection-config.test.ts` / main oauth guard tests already covering the three strings — assert latch flag reaches renderer.
- Regression: `message-render-boundary.test.tsx` + a shell-level test that lookup OOB during reconnect does not unmount the app root to blank.
- Manual: macOS Desktop + remote OAuth → revoke session → relaunch → must show recovery, not white void.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Cold launch with expired remote OAuth never leaves a blank white window for more than a brief paint; recovery UI with Sign in is visible.
- [ ] Log phrases for expired session / not signed in / WS ticket failure each map to actionable recovery (not infinite silent retry only).
- [ ] User can open Gateway settings and switch to Local without quitting.
- [ ] Successful re-sign-in clears reauth latch and reaches a normal chat shell.
- [ ] `useClientLookup` OOB and `Composer is not available` do not white-out the entire app.
- [ ] Transport-only ticket failures still retry; pure auth failures do not spin forever without UI.

## Priority

**P0** — app unusable on launch for remote OAuth users after session expiry (common after idle / update / remote restart).

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop client renderer/GPU processes spin at 100%+ CPU at idle — constant re-render loop, high energy usage

labels.name: area/usage-cost
labels.description: Token accounting, usage reporting, billing, cost tracking

items.body:
## Summary
The Hermes desktop (Electron) client pins the Renderer and GPU helper processes at
50–90% CPU even when idle (no active generation, no user input). The macOS battery/
power menu reports Hermes as the highest energy consumer and the machine gets
noticeably hot. Quitting and reopening the app does NOT resolve it — the spin
returns within seconds of launch.

## Environment
- Hermes Agent (Python core) version: **0.19.0**
- Desktop app (Electron, affected layer) version: **0.18.0**
  (from `Hermes.app/Contents/Info.plist` → CFBundleShortVersionString)
- Platform: macOS 26.5.2 (Apple Silicon, arm64)
- Install: `/Users/<user>/.hermes/hermes-agent/apps/desktop/release/mac-arm64/Hermes.app`
- image_gen config (for context, not the cause):
  ```yaml
  image_gen:
    use_gateway: true
    model: fal-ai/gpt-image-2
    provider: fal
  ```

## Reproduction
1. Launch the Hermes desktop client.
2. Do nothing (no chat, no image generation).
3. Open Activity Monitor and sort by %CPU, or run `top` / `ps aux`.
4. Observe `Hermes Helper (Renderer)` and `Hermes Helper` (GPU) processes
   holding 50–90% CPU continuously.

The loop is present from startup (PID elapsed time ~10s already shows 70%+)
and is reproducible across restarts.

## Evidence

Real-time process CPU (measured twice ~10s apart, both readings high):
| Process | CPU #1 | CPU #2 |
|---|---|---|
| Hermes Helper (Renderer) | 67.4% | 87.4% |
| Hermes Helper (GPU)      | 56.6% | 53.9% |
| Hermes main process      | 0.4%  | 0.1%  |
| **Total Hermes**         | ~109% |       |

`sample` of the Renderer process main thread (2s) shows the main thread
stuck inside V8 continuous JIT/compile + IPC, never yielding — a classic
front-end render loop:
```
1577 Thread_...: com.apple.main-thread (serial)
+ 1577 ElectronMain
+   v8::internal::compiler::CompilationDependencies::DependOnContextCell
+     v8::Value::IsFunction()
+       mach_msg  (blocked on IPC, repeated 1203x in 2s sample)
```
The GPU helper is pinned by `CVDisplayLink` (per-display-refresh compositing)
with a continuously queued Metal command stream — i.e. the UI re-composites
every frame even while idle.

Note: the backend (`hermes serve` / `hermes gateway`) stays at ~0.1% CPU,
so this is purely a front-end (Electron renderer) issue, not model inference.
Image generation itself runs in the fal.ai cloud (`use_gateway: true`); the
local cost is only decoding/rendering the returned image, which is amplified
by the pre-existing idle spin.

## Expected
When idle, the desktop client should consume near-0% CPU and not appear as a
top energy user in the macOS power menu.

## Actual
Renderer + GPU helpers sustain 50–90% CPU indefinitely from launch, causing
constant fan/heat and high energy impact.

## Suspected cause (for triage)
A self-triggering re-render loop in the front-end (e.g. a component that
mutates its own state during render, or a polling/heartbeat subscription that
fires whole-page re-renders with `--disable-background-timer-throttling`
enabled). Happy to provide full `sample` output or spindump if helpful.

items.title: Desktop startup fails with GIL stall on Windows — _warm_gateway_module() import blocks event loop 15-22s

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

labels.name: comp/dashboard
labels.description: Web dashboard / control panel UI (dashboard/, landing)

items.body:
## Problem

Hermes Desktop on Windows fails to start and shows Could not connect to Hermes gateway on the error screen, even though the messaging gateway (Weixin/Feishu) runs fine independently.

## Root Cause

On Windows with Python 3.11, hermes serve has a _warm_gateway_module() function that imports hermes_cli.gateway via run_in_executor. This import triggers heavy C-level .pyc file reads that do not release the GIL, freezing the asyncio event loop for 15-22 seconds during backend startup.

Meanwhile, the Desktop Electron app probes the backend WebSocket with a 10-second timeout. The probe fails because the event loop is blocked by the GIL, and the WebSocket ready frame can never be sent.

## GUI Log Evidence

```## Problem

Hermes Desktop on Windows fails to start and shows Could not connect to Hermes gateway on the error screen, even though the messaging gateway runs fine independently.

## Root Cause

On Windows with Python 3.11, hermes serve has a _warm_gateway_module() that imports hermes_cli.gateway via run_in_executor. This import triggers heavy C-level .pyc file reads that do not release the GIL, freezing the asyncio event loop for 15-22 seconds.

Meanwhile, the Desktop Electron app probes the WebSocket with a 10-second timeout. The probe fails because the event loop is blocked by the GIL.

GUI log evidence:
2026-07-28 10:54:13,929 Desktop cron scheduler started
2026-07-28 10:54:31,078 event loop stalled 15.2s
2026-07-28 10:54:31,131 ws accepted
2026-07-28 10:54:31,
2026-07-28 10:54:13,929 Desktop cron scheduler started
2026-07-28 10:54:31,078 event loop stalled 15.2s (GIL pressure suspected)
2026-07-28 10:54:31,131 ws accepted peer=...
2026-07-28 10:54:31,148 ws send failed peer=... error_type=WebSocketDisconnect
2026-07-28 10:54:31,148 ERROR ws ready frame send failed peer=...
```

## Fix

Move _warm_gateway_module() from the background executor to a synchronous call before the lifespan yield, so the GIL block is absorbed during backend initialization before the event loop accepts connections.

In hermes_cli/web_server.py, _lifespan():

OLD:
asyncio.get_event_loop().run_in_executor(None, _warm_gateway_module)

NEW:
_warm_gateway_module()

## Environment

OS: Windows 10
Python: 3.11.15
Hermes: v0.19.0

items.title: Dashboard chat MCP discovery crashes: signal.signal() runs at import from a worker thread (ValueError: signal only works in main thread)

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

labels.name: comp/dashboard
labels.description: Web dashboard / control panel UI (dashboard/, landing)

items.body:
### Environment
- Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20), Docker deployment (Linux, s6-supervised dashboard).
- Surfaces as: the browser dashboard chat shows **"MCP Servers (0) connected"** and the agent has no MCP tools, while the dashboard's MCP admin page shows the same servers connected.

### What happens
`tui_gateway/entry.py` installs signal handlers at **module import time** (~line 188):

```python
if hasattr(signal, "SIGPIPE"):
    signal.signal(signal.SIGPIPE, signal.SIG_IGN)
if hasattr(signal, "SIGTERM"):
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, _log_signal)
```

`tui_gateway/server.py:_build()` (~line 1866) imports that module lazily
(`from tui_gateway.entry import ensure_mcp_discovery_started`) from a
**worker thread**, not the main thread. CPython only permits
`signal.signal()` on the main thread, so the import raises and MCP
discovery for the dashboard chat never starts:

```
WARNING tui_gateway.server: MCP discovery startup failed
  File ".../tui_gateway/server.py", line 1866, in _build
    from tui_gateway.entry import ensure_mcp_discovery_started
  File ".../tui_gateway/entry.py", line 188, in <module>
    signal.signal(signal.SIGPIPE, signal.SIG_IGN)
ValueError: signal only works in main thread of the main interpreter
```

It repeats on every chat build, so the dashboard-embedded chat is
consistently left with zero MCP servers.

### Minimal repro (no deployment specifics)
```python
# mod_with_signals.py
import signal
signal.signal(signal.SIGPIPE, signal.SIG_IGN)   # runs at import time

# repro.py
import threading
def work():
    import mod_with_signals            # imported off the main thread
t = threading.Thread(target=work)
t.start(); t.join()
# -> ValueError: signal only works in main thread of the main interpreter
```

### Suggested fix
Guard the signal installs so they no-op off the main thread, or move them
out of import scope into an explicit init function invoked from the main
thread:

```python
import threading
if threading.current_thread() is threading.main_thread():
    if hasattr(signal, "SIGPIPE"):
        signal.signal(signal.SIGPIPE, signal.SIG_IGN)
    if hasattr(signal, "SIGTERM"):
        signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, _log_signal)
```

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop — opening chat in existing Project still auto-creates path-named Projects (e.g. lib/…)

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
### Bug Description

Opening or working in a chat that already belongs to an **existing named Desktop Project** still causes Hermes to **auto-create / auto-promote additional top-level Projects** in the sidebar. The new rows show up with path-style labels (parent/child), e.g. `…/HERMES` and `lib/hermes-agent`, instead of keeping the work under the Project the user already opened.

Impact: the Projects list becomes noisy and misleading. Sessions that the user thinks are “inside Project A” appear to spawn sibling Projects, and the sidebar no longer reflects the curated project the user chose.

This is distinct from the request to *optionally disable* home-dir git discovery (#64615): even with an explicit Project already open, nested / related paths still mint new auto-project rows.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. In Hermes Desktop, create (or use) a **named Project** whose folders cover a real workspace tree (multi-folder or monorepo-style layout is enough).
2. Open an existing chat that already sits under that Project (or start a new chat **inside** that Project).
3. Work normally — including any agent activity that `cd`s into a nested folder / nested git root under or beside the Project’s folders (e.g. a nested package path such as `lib/…`).
4. Return to the Projects overview / sidebar.

### Expected Behavior

- Opening a chat already bound to Project A does **not** create new top-level Projects.
- Nested folders and nested git roots under Project A’s folders stay **lanes/repos inside Project A** (or remain invisible as top-level Projects).
- Auto-discovery / session-derived auto-projects must not promote paths that an explicit Project already owns (longest-prefix folder match).
- Path-disambiguated labels like `parent/child` must not appear as new top-level Projects when the user is already inside a named Project that covers that work.

### Actual Behavior

- New top-level Project rows appear automatically with path-style names, e.g.:
  - `HERMES-DESKTOP-SERC/HERMES` (path-prefixed auto label)
  - `lib/hermes-agent` (path-prefixed auto label)
- These look like auto-promoted repo/cwd roots (`isAuto: true`), not intentional user creates from the New Project dialog.
- The session that was opened under the existing Project can effectively “leak” into, or sit alongside, these phantom auto-projects.

### Affected Component

- **Hermes Desktop** — Projects sidebar / session grouping
- Backend tree builder + discovery:
  - `tui_gateway/project_tree.py` — `build_tree` Tier 2 (session-derived auto) + Tier 3 (discovered repos) + `_disambiguate_labels`
  - `tui_gateway/server.py` — `projects.record_repos`, `_discover_repos_payload`, junk filters
  - `apps/desktop/src/store/projects.ts` — `scanAndRecordRepos`, `followActiveSessionCwd`, `projectIdForCwd`
  - `apps/desktop/electron/git-repo-scan.ts` — home/root git scan
- Related agent surface (only if agent called create; secondary): `tools/project_tools.py` `project_create` — but path-style `parent/child` labels match **auto disambiguation**, not a human `name=` from the create dialog.

### Root Cause Analysis

| What | File | Symbol / detail |
|------|------|-----------------|
| Auto projects from unowned sessions | `tui_gateway/project_tree.py` | `build_tree` Tier 2 (~L618–698): leftover sessions whose cwd/repo is **not** claimed by `_project_for_session` become top-level auto projects (`is_auto=True`, id = root path) |
| Auto projects from disk scan | `tui_gateway/project_tree.py` | Tier 3 (~L700–724): `discovered_repos` not owned by an explicit project become empty auto projects |
| Path-style labels | `tui_gateway/project_tree.py` | `_disambiguate_labels` (~L301–325): colliding basenames grow into `parent/child` labels — matches reported names like `lib/hermes-agent` |
| Ownership gate | `tui_gateway/project_tree.py` | `_FolderIndex` + `_project_for_session` (~L450–500): longest-prefix match on project **folders only**. If the live session cwd / git common-dir resolves to a path **outside** the Project’s folder list (nested sibling root, agent `cd`, worktree outside folders, remote path spelling mismatch), the session is treated as **unowned** → Tier 2 mints a new auto Project |
| Scan feed | `apps/desktop/src/store/projects.ts` | `scanAndRecordRepos` → `projects.record_repos` refreshes Tier 3 candidates whenever Projects UI loads |
| Cwd follow | `apps/desktop/src/store/projects.ts` | `followActiveSessionCwd` refreshes tree after agent cwd moves — surfaces the newly minted auto project immediately |

```python
# tui_gateway/project_tree.py — Tier 2 auto mint (smoking gun shape)
result.append(
    _project_node(
        pid=auto_root,
        label=base_name(auto_root) or auto_root,
        path=auto_root,
        ...,
        is_auto=True,
    )
)
# then:
_disambiguate_labels([p for p in result if p.get("isAuto")])
# → labels become "lib/hermes-agent", "…/HERMES", etc.
```

Likely failure modes to fix as a class (not just one path):

1. **Ownership miss**: session under/near Project A fails `_project_for_session` → auto Project.
2. **Nested git root**: nested repo root is not under any registered folder string → Tier 2/3 promotes it even when the user is “in” the parent Project.
3. **Discovery noise**: home scan records extra roots; Tier 3 shows them as Projects even while an explicit Project is active/open.
4. **Disambiguation cosmetics**: once two autos share a basename, labels become path-looking names that look like “new projects the user never created.”

### Proposed Fix

1. **Hard ownership rule:** if a session’s cwd **or** resolved git common-dir is under any folder of an explicit (non-archived) Project, **never** emit a Tier 2 auto project for that root. Prefer attaching as a repo/lane under the owning Project (seed folder repos / nested-repo handling) or keep the session in that Project without a new top-level row.
2. **Tier 3 gate while inside a Project (optional product choice):** do not surface zero-session discovered roots that are ancestors/descendants/siblings covered by an explicit Project’s folders; at minimum, suppress roots already claimed by `_project_for_path`.
3. **Nested roots under a Project folder:** fold nested git roots into the parent Project’s `repos[]` instead of minting a sibling auto Project (see related nested/monorepo pain in #70790).
4. **Do not treat agent `cd` as project create:** `tools/project_tools.py` already documents create/switch as intentional; ensure cwd moves only call `followActiveSessionCwd` / tree refresh, never `projects.create` / auto-promote outside ownership.
5. **Tests** (pure `build_tree` fixtures — no live git required):
   - Explicit Project with folder `/ws/app`; session cwd `/ws/app/lib/pkg` → **no** auto project; session scoped to Project.
   - Nested git root under Project folder → one Project, nested repo node, **no** second top-level auto.
   - Two unowned repos both named `hermes-agent` → disambiguated labels OK, but neither appears if an explicit Project owns both paths.
   - Opening/refreshing Projects view with discovery on does not add autos for roots already under explicit Project folders.

```python
# sketch: after computing repo_root / cwd for unowned sessions
owner = _project_for_path(folder_index, root) or _project_for_path(folder_index, cwd)
if owner:
    by_project.setdefault(owner["id"], []).append(session)
    continue  # never _add_auto
```

### Tests

- [ ] `tui_gateway` / project_tree unit tests: ownership prevents Tier 2 auto when cwd is under explicit Project folder
- [ ] Nested git root under Project folder does not create a second top-level `isAuto` node
- [ ] Tier 3 discovered root already under explicit Project folders is skipped (already partially gated by `_project_for_path` at L709 — extend coverage for nested / prefix edge cases)
- [ ] Regression: true unowned external repos still become auto projects (Home / discovery still works)
- [ ] Desktop: open chat in named Project → tree refresh → project count for autos does not increase for in-tree paths

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Opening a chat that already belongs to named Project A never creates a new top-level Project row for paths under A’s folders
- [ ] Nested package / nested git paths (e.g. `lib/…`) do not appear as separate top-level Projects when covered by A
- [ ] Path-style auto labels (`parent/child`) only appear for genuinely unowned external repos, not for work inside an open explicit Project
- [ ] Agent `cd` / cwd follow refreshes grouping inside A; it does not mint sibling Projects
- [ ] Unrelated external repos can still auto-surface when not covered by any explicit Project (unless discovery is disabled per #64615)
- [ ] No change to intentional `project_create` / New Project dialog behavior

### Operating System

macOS / Linux — Hermes Desktop (Projects sidebar). UI-repro; no debug paste required for the core grouping bug.

### Environment / version

Hermes Desktop current `main` / latest app build. Grouping logic lives in gateway `projects.tree` + Desktop `scanAndRecordRepos`.

### Priority

P2 — data-model / sidebar correctness; confuses project identity every time users work in multi-folder trees.

### Related (not duplicates)

- #64615 — feature: disable automatic project/repo discovery entirely (opt-out). This bug is **incorrect auto-promotion while already inside an explicit Project**, not only “discovery exists.”
- #70790 — nested Hermes project inherits umbrella monorepo worktree lanes (same nested-tree family; different symptom).
- #53004 — Projects paradigm broke folder → session flow (broader; cite only).

### Debug Report

N/A — pure Desktop Projects grouping / auto-promotion UI bug; reproducible from sidebar state without log paste.

items.title: Successful managed-runtime repair leaves venv.stale.runtime-* behind permanently (1.1 GB per repair)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: needs-decision
labels.description: Awaiting maintainer decision before any implementation

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Summary

A successful managed-Python runtime repair parks the previous venv next to the live one as `venv.stale.runtime-<token>` and nothing ever reclaims it. Every repair leaves a complete venv on disk, permanently.

Found one at 1.1 GB — five times the size of the live venv it replaced — and only by chance.

```
$ du -sh ~/src/hermes-agent/venv*
1.1G    /Users/francip/src/hermes-agent/venv.stale.runtime-1785210060-74567-8ca026cc
222M    /Users/francip/src/hermes-agent/venv
```

## Why it happens

`_cut_over_candidate()` in `hermes_cli/managed_uv.py` parks the live venv before promoting the candidate:

```python
backup = live.with_name(f"{live.name}.stale.runtime-{token}")
```

On success it returns that path as `RuntimeRepairResult.backup_venv` and prints:

```
ℹ Previous venv parked at <name>; keep it until all older Hermes processes have exited.
```

Parking it is correct — it is the rollback path, and long-lived processes may still be mapped into it. The gap is that nothing ever completes the lifecycle:

- `_remove_tree()` is boundary-constrained (`path.resolve().relative_to(boundary.resolve())`) to the runtime dir, while the backup deliberately lives at project root — so it can never be a removal candidate.
- No later `hermes update` sweeps older `venv.stale.runtime-*` directories.
- `hermes doctor` does not mention or offer to reclaim them.
- The existing `venv.stale.runtime-*` assertions in `tests/hermes_cli/test_managed_uv.py` cover the interrupt and rollback paths (no orphan when the cut-over aborts). The success path has no counterpart.

The instruction to keep it is also open-ended: "until all older Hermes processes have exited" is a condition the user is left to evaluate, with no command that answers it and no reminder afterwards. In practice the directory is simply forgotten.

## Expected behavior

Reclaim it once nothing holds it. Any of:

- At the start of the next `hermes update`, remove `venv.stale.runtime-*` directories that no live process is using (the holder detection needed for this overlaps with #70201).
- Report them in `hermes doctor`, with a `--fix` to remove them.
- Keep only the most recent, dropping older ones on the next repair.

## Reproduction

1. Run a `hermes update` that triggers a managed Python runtime repair (here: SQLite 3.50.4 → 3.53.1).
2. Observe the "Previous venv parked at ..." line.
3. Restart long-lived processes so nothing holds the old venv.
4. `ls -d ~/src/hermes-agent/venv*` — the parked copy is still there, and stays there indefinitely.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20), upstream ef267011
- macOS 26.5 (Darwin 25.5.0), Python 3.11
- Managed uv/Python runtime, editable install at `~/src/hermes-agent`

items.title: [ready-for-agent] Execute authorized Luxiaonan WAV cleanup and verify reclaimed space
items.body:
## Parent

#73049

## What to build

Execute the separately authorized one-time cleanup for the exact Luxiaonan transcript WAV cache bundle, then prove the real post-action machine state. The action must consume a fresh owner-bound cleanup preflight, remove only the 101 approved WAV targets, preserve all retained transcript segments and source media, and immediately run the existing post-action verifier.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Blocked ticket #73058 is complete locally and the current post-action verifier bytes pass their canonical code-patch and independent-review gates.
- [ ] A fresh highest-level owner-specific preflight recomputes the exact 101 WAV targets, exact hashes, 101 protected retained artifacts, 101 source mappings, handles, graph bindings, and candidate bytes immediately before mutation.
- [ ] Any VETO, count/hash drift, open handle, graph/live mismatch, unapproved dependency, protected-artifact inclusion, source ambiguity, retained-consumer failure, or authorization-scope mismatch stops the action with no deletion.
- [ ] The execution deletes only the exact preflight-bound WAV targets; transcript segments, source videos, workspaces, memory stores, dependency-graph state, and unrelated files remain untouched.
- [ ] The real post-action verifier reports all 101 targets absent, all 101 retained segment identities unchanged, the actual downstream consumer passing across the expected rows, and reclaimed free space within the approved filesystem tolerance.
- [ ] A machine-validated cleanup scoreback is persisted, binding the preflight, exact action set, post-action receipt, reclaimed bytes, and no-out-of-scope-mutation evidence.
- [ ] Final independent read-only review finds no replayable counterexample on the frozen receipts and exact action digest.
- [ ] No daemon, watcher, hook, background job, alternate cleanup authority, automatic future deletion, branch, push, or PR is introduced.

## Blocked by

- #73058

## Stop condition

Stop before deletion on any fresh preflight VETO. After deletion, do not claim completion unless the post-action verifier and scoreback both pass. This ticket is the single explicit destructive action authorized by the current user Goal; it does not create standing deletion authority.

## Triage

ready-for-agent (the repository does not expose this label to the submitting account, so readiness is preserved in the title).
